entries.new: visa on arrival, 30 days for the 17 the official list names; embassy visa for the 11 it does not
entries.note: The only official page we can read publishes one list and one allowance — 'may be issued a 30 day visitor visa on arrival' — and says citizens of all other countries need a visa before arrival. Publishing 90 days visa-free contradicted our own cited source. The eleven nationalities the list does not name are settled on the side that cannot mislead: a traveller who arranges a visa they did not need loses a fee, one who flies expecting entry loses the trip.

entries.reason: The business e-visa was cited to the tourist notice, which states a 28-day stay — the tourist visa's, not this one's. It now cites the business notice, which is the authority's own page for this visa and does not print the stay length, so it carries the official-portal mark.

entries.new: 90 days
entries.note: The official page states the visa is issued for 30, 60 or 90 days depending on the itinerary; we published the shortest of the three as though it were the only one.

entries.field: National (type D) visa fee — long stay, student, digital nomad, work
entries.new: 90 EUR
entries.note: Orden AUC/891/2024 raised the national long-stay visa fee to 90 euros, equalising it with the EU uniform visa fee after the Visa Code increase of June 2024. Our figure was the previous order's.

entries.reason: The 6,300 NOK figure is stated in the immigration regulation itself — § 17-10 first paragraph (a), "kr 6 300 i saker om arbeid eller studier" — rather than only on UDI's front page.

entries.field: National (type D) visa fee — residency, D7, D8, student, work
entries.new: 110 EUR
entries.note: Portaria n.º 91/2025/1 raised the national visa fee to 110 euros in March 2025; its own preamble notes the 90-euro figure had stood since 2011. Ours was the 2011 figure.

entries.field: Hong Kong, Serbia, South Korea, Türkiye — visa-free rows
entries.new: visa-free, with the portal's silence stated in the note
entries.note: The Immigration Agency's e-visa portal publishes a visa-free list of 60 nationalities that names Macau but not Hong Kong, and none of Serbia, South Korea or Türkiye, each of which we record under a bilateral arrangement. The portal's other column does not render for any reader we have, so we cannot tell absence from omission — the rows stand and the reader is told what the official list says.

entries.field: US-visa holders from China, the Dominican Republic and India
entries.old: AVE electronic authorization, 90 days, for Chinese and Dominican holders of a US or Schengen visa
entries.new: Visa-free with a valid US visa, no AVE: Dominican and Indian citizens 90 days (tourism), Chinese citizens 30 days (tourism or business); India added; Schengen visas do not qualify
entries.note: Resolución 316/2025 (in force since July 2025) lets Chinese and Dominican citizens with a US visa in a similar category enter without a consular visa or an AVE, and Resolución 353/2025 (August 2025) does the same for Indian citizens. The Migraciones AVE page repeats both. Neither resolution mentions Schengen visas. We still published the older AVE route, which is no longer how these three nationalities enter.

entries.field: Chinese and Indian citizens: AVE eligibility
entries.old: AVE available to holders of a US or Schengen visa
entries.new: Not on the AVE list; a valid US visa gives visa-free entry instead (CN 30 days, IN 90 days)
entries.note: The AVE page says Chinese citizens no longer need an AVE if they hold a US visa or green card, and that Indian citizens travelling for tourism with a US visa enter without one. Neither country appears on the page's list of nationalities eligible for the AVE.

entries.field: AVE qualifying visa for Filipino, Indonesian and Vietnamese citizens
entries.new: valid US visa
entries.note: The AVE page requires, 'de manera excluyente', a valid US visa in category B2, J, B1, O, P, E or H-1B. It does not mention Schengen visas. The same correction is made in the summary and in the AVE fee note.

entries.new: multiple
entries.note: The page gives a stay of three months from the first entry, 'permitiendo múltiples entradas y salidas'.

entries.reason: The cash limits were cited to ARCA's front page, which does not state them. ARCA's travellers' page on bringing money in and out states the USD 10,000 threshold and the USD 5,000 limit for under-16s.

entries.old: USD 10,000 or more declared on arrival and departure; USD 5,000 limit for travelers aged 16 and under
entries.new: USD 10,000 or more declared on arrival; USD 10,000 or more can leave only by bank transfer, not in cash; USD 5,000 limit for travelers under 16
entries.note: ARCA says larger sums require the OM 2249A declaration on entry and must leave by bank transfer. The lower limit is for 'menores de 16 años', meaning under 16, not 16 and under.

entries.new: AUD 250
entries.note: Home Affairs now prices the Tourist stream (apply outside Australia) "From AUD250.00", read on the subclass 600 page and repeated in the sidebar of the 601 and 651 pages. Lower charges for Pacific Island and Timor-Leste citizens apply from 1 July 2026.

entries.new: AUD 840
entries.note: The First Working Holiday visa stream now shows AUD840.00, read twice today; the second and third visas show AUD1,000.00.

entries.reason: The cited page is the consular portal's index and states no country's regime; the Foreign Ministry's own table of entry visas (Quadro Geral de Regime de Vistos, updated August 26, 2026), linked two levels below it, states the regime and permitted stay for every nationality.
The cited page does not state the eVisa's fee or validity; the official eVisa portal's tourist-visa page states both ($80.90; valid 5 or 10 years, multiple entries).
The cited page does not state a passport-validity rule; the official eVisa portal's FAQ does, in so many words.
The cited page is Receita Federal's front page and does not state the cash threshold; the Traveller's Guide page on cash at entry does.
The cited page is the Ministry of Health's front page; its vaccination-for-travellers page states that no proof of vaccination is required for entry and when yellow fever vaccination is recommended.

entries.field: Chinese and Indonesian citizens: entry regime
entries.new: Visa-free, up to 30 days
entries.note: The Foreign Ministry's visa table (updated August 26, 2026) marks both with code 2: visa exemption for up to 30 days. The FAQ's example of a nationality needing a consular visa no longer names Chinese citizens.

entries.new: Visa-free, up to 60 days

entries.field: Armenian, Belizean, Bosnian, Grenadian, Micronesian, Moldovan, Mongolian, Namibian, Kittitian, Saint Lucian and Vincentian citizens: entry regime
entries.new: Visa-free, up to 90 days

entries.field: Albanian, Dominican (Dominica) and Georgian citizens: entry regime
entries.new: Visa-free, up to 90 days in any 180-day period

entries.old: 90 days, extendable once by the Federal Police to 180 days per 12 months
entries.new: 90 days in any 180-day period
entries.note: The visa table marks these nationalities' exemption with an asterisk: 'Maximum stay of 90 days every 180 days'. Germany and Italy, marked the same way, already said so; the extendable-days figure is removed from France, the Netherlands, Switzerland and Ukraine.

entries.old: At least 6 months, required for eVisa applications
entries.new: At least one month after arrival (6 months still recommended)
entries.note: The eVisa portal: 'Your passport must be valid for at least one more month after your arrival in Brazil', with a caution to check the airline accepts it.
Receita Federal states 'montante superior a US$ 10.000,00 ou o equivalente em outra moeda' on both entry and exit, under Law 14.286 of 2021.

entries.old: Enter only with an organized, locally-vetted guide
entries.new: Avoid all favelas, including tours marketed to tourists
entries.note: The FCDO's safety page tells visitors to 'avoid all favelas, including favela tours marketed to tourists'. The level is unchanged.

entries.reason: Proof of funds: the Visit Canada landing page does not state it; IRCC's 'Who can apply' page lists 'have enough money for your stay' among the basic entry requirements and says the amount varies with the length and kind of stay.

entries.new: visa-free, 30 days
entries.note: The Consular Department's visa-free FAQ lists the UK among the 50 countries whose ordinary passports enter visa-free for up to 30 days, in force until December 31, 2026; the FCDO's China entry page says the same. The summary and the visa-free FAQ now name the UK.

entries.new: visa-free, 30 days
entries.note: Canada is on the same 50-country list, in force until December 31, 2026. The summary and the visa-free FAQ now name Canada.

entries.field: Greece, Cyprus, Slovenia, Brunei — entry requirement
entries.new: visa-free, 30 days
entries.note: All four are on the Ministry's 50-country unilateral list; we had them as needing a visa. Brunei's exemption has no end date, the other three run to December 31, 2026.

entries.new: in force until December 31, 2027
entries.note: The date we published had passed; the Ministry's FAQ gives the Russian exemption a separate end date from the other 48 countries.

entries.old: announced for one year initially (from June 1, 2025)
entries.new: in force until December 31, 2026

entries.field: Albania, Antigua and Barbuda, Georgia, Maldives, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Suriname, Uzbekistan — entry requirement
entries.new: visa-free, 30 days
entries.note: The Ministry's Mutual Visa Exemption List shows an agreement covering ordinary passports in force for each (Albania 2023, Antigua and Barbuda 2024, Georgia 2024, Maldives 2022, Samoa 2025, Solomon Islands 2024, Suriname 2014, Uzbekistan 2025). The list's own note says stays under these agreements are generally limited to 30 days.

entries.old: trial unilateral visa-free entry announced in 2025
entries.new: mutual visa exemption agreement
entries.note: Azerbaijan is not on the unilateral list; the mutual list shows its ordinary-passport agreement in force from July 16, 2025. The 30-day stay is unchanged.

entries.field: 240-hour visa-free transit — eligibility stated on visa-required rows
entries.new: removed from rows whose nationality is not among the 57 eligible
entries.note: The immigration administration's transit page lists 57 eligible countries. A shared note on 103 visa-required rows (AF, DZ, AO, BD, BZ, BJ, BT, BO, BW, BF, BI, CV, KH, CM, CF, TD, CO, KM, CR, CI, CU, CD, DJ, DO, EC, EG, SV, GQ, ER, SZ, ET, GA, GM, GH, GT, GN, GW, GY, HT, HN, IR, IQ, IL, JM, JO, KE, KI, XK, LA, LB, LS, LR, LY, MG, MW, ML, MH, MR, FM, MD, MN, MA, MZ, MM, NA, NR, NP, NI, NE, KP, PW, PS, PA, PG, PY, CG, RW, KN, LC, VC, ST, SN, SL, SO, SS, LK, SD, SY, TJ, TZ, TL, TG, TT, TN, TM, TV, UG, VU, VA, VE, YE, ZM, ZW) offered the transit to nationalities that are not on it.

entries.old: listed for Türkiye; missing for UA, VN, CZ, KG, LT
entries.new: removed for Türkiye; added for UA, VN, CZ, KG, LT
entries.note: Türkiye is not among the 57; Kyrgyzstan and Vietnam were added on August 20, 2026 (NIA announcement 2026 No. 4), and Ukraine, Czechia and Lithuania were already on the list.

entries.reason: The unilateral visa-free rows cited the consular site's front page, which states none of them. They now cite the same site's visa-free FAQ, which names all 50 countries, the 30-day stay and each scheme's end date. Russia and Brazil moved here from www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/, and the rows that had leaned on the default source now carry it explicitly.

Rows visa-free under a mutual exemption agreement now cite the Ministry's Mutual Visa Exemption List, which names each agreement, the passports it covers and its date of entry into force. Armenia, San Marino and Mauritius keep the default source: the list does not state their longer stays.
The 240-hour transit cited the immigration administration's front page; its own policy page states the 57 eligible countries and the 10-day limit.
Customs' passenger clearance guide states the declaration thresholds (RMB 20,000 in cash, or foreign currency equivalent to US$5,000); the front page cited before does not.

The cited page now redirects to the ministry's list of visa types, which names no nationalities; the ministry's "¿Necesito una visa?" page publishes Lists A, B and C of exempt passports, in so many words.
The cited page does not state the Visitor visa fee; the ministry's cost table, filtered to Visitante – Turismo, does.
The cited page does not state the passport or onward-ticket rules; the FCDO's entry-requirements page does, in so many words.

entries.field: Twelve passports we sent to the Visitor visa
entries.new: Visa-free, 90 days
entries.note: The Cancillería's List A of passports exempt from a short-stay visa names Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bhutan, Indonesia, Morocco, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Oman, the Philippines and Serbia, and List B names Hong Kong SAR.

entries.new: eVisa — Visitor (V) visa, with a conditional exemption
entries.note: The Cancillería places Nicaragua on List C (conditional exemption), not List A; only natives of the Caribbean Coast autonomous regions holding a US or Schengen visa or residence permit are named as exempt.

entries.new: 56 USD
entries.note: The cost table lists Visitante – Turismo at USD 56 study plus USD 82 issuance (EUR 44 + EUR 63 in Europe and Cuba).

entries.new: Valid on entry; 6 months beyond departure recommended
entries.note: The FCDO states the passport must be valid on entry, and that Colombian immigration authorities recommend an expiry date at least 6 months after the date you plan to leave.

entries.new: tourist eVisa, 90 days
entries.note: The eVisa portal read on 31 August listed 66 eligible countries; on 25 September it lists 68, and the two it added are Guyana and Kosovo. Only the eVisa is recorded for them: the portal does not say whether the visa on arrival extends to the same two.

entries.new: USD 50

entries.field: Tourist visa validity, stay and entries

entries.note: Read on 31 August the page said single entry, valid 90 days; on 25 September it says multiple entries, valid for a period of 1 year, permitted stay each entry 3 months.

entries.field: AVE eligibility — 66 nationalities (AL, AO, AG, SA, BS, BH, BZ, BJ, BW, BN, BF, BI, BT, CV, KH, CM, CI, CU, ER, SZ, ET, GA, GM, GH, GN, GQ, GW, MH, SB, KE, KI, LA, LS, MG, MW, MV, MU, MD, MZ, MM, NA, NR, NP, NE, OM, PW, PG, CF, CG, CD, RW, WS, ST, SN, SC, SL, TW, TZ, TG, TO, TV, UG, VU, DJ, ZM, ZW)
entries.new: embassy visa, or the AVE electronic travel authorization for holders of a valid US visa (tourist-embassy, ave)
entries.note: The Migraciones AVE page lists 69 nationalities under "Habilitados para AVE". Three (Philippines, Indonesia, Vietnam) already carried the AVE option; the other 66 showed only a consular visa. The page makes the AVE available for tourism to ordinary-passport holders of a current US visa in category B2, J, B1, O, P (P1-P2-P3), E or H-1B, so these rows now offer it the way the existing AVE rows do.

entries.old: not listed (visitor's visa from a mission, or the eVisa pilot)
entries.new: ETA added: online at eta.dha.gov.za, outcome typically within 24 hours, stays of up to 90 days extendable by 90 through the platform, arrivals at OR Tambo, Cape Town, King Shaka and Lanseria airports only; fee not published
entries.note: President Ramaphosa officially launched the ETA on 12 August 2026. The Minister's address says it was piloted for travellers from China, India, Indonesia and Mexico during the G20 Presidency, has processed 216 204 applications, and will 'progressively become compulsory' for visa-required countries, with embassies told as countries are added. Visa-exempt travellers may use it voluntarily. No fee appears in any official source we could read, so none is published.

entries.field: China, India, Indonesia and Mexico: application routes
entries.old: visitor's visa from a South African mission (plus the eVisa for China and India)
entries.new: still visa-required; the ETA is now also open to these four nationalities, alongside the mission route
entries.note: Requirement unchanged: the sources say the ETA is not yet compulsory and the ETA portal's own FAQ still points unsuccessful applicants to missions and the eVisa. Which other visa-required nationalities have been added since the launch is not published, so no other row was changed.

entries.field: Visa-free stay for citizens of Poland, Lithuania and Latvia
entries.new: 90 days from the date of entry (90 days per calendar year cap unchanged)
entries.note: The Foreign Ministry's page on the European visa-free regime says the stay is 30 days from entry for the 38 listed states, but 'for citizens of Poland, Lithuania and Latvia (including holders of Latvia's non-citizen status), the permitted stay is extended to 90 days'; the regime runs until 31 December 2026. We had all three at 30. Checked while following up the MFA's switch to new Visa Regulations (Council of Ministers Resolution No. 464 of 14 September 2026, published on pravo.by 17 September, replacing Resolution No. 1065 of 2010): the new rules leave our type C and D figures as they were: C valid up to 90 days, D multiple-entry and usually one year, a decision in 3 to 5 working days or 2 when urgent, a 60-euro fee on the MFA fee page, and EUR 10,000 insurance on the airport page.

entries.field: AVE row notes — 69 nationalities (PH, ID, VN, AL, AO, AG, BS, BH, BZ, BJ, BT, BW, BN, BF, BI, CV, KH, CM, CF, CI, CU, CD, DJ, GQ, ER, SZ, ET, GA, GM, GH, GN, GW, KE, KI, LA, LS, MG, MW, MV, MH, MU, MD, MZ, MM, NA, NR, NP, NE, OM, PW, PG, CG, RW, WS, ST, SA, SN, SC, SL, SB, TW, TZ, TG, TO, TV, UG, VU, ZM, ZW)
entries.old: Consular tourist visa required. Holders of a valid US visa may qualify for the AVE electronic travel authorization instead. Confirm eligibility with the Argentine consulate or Migraciones before booking.
entries.new: Consular tourist visa required. For tourism, ordinary-passport holders with a current US visa in category B2, B1, J, O, P (P1–P3), E or H-1B can apply online for the AVE electronic travel authorization instead; the US visa must stay valid through AVE processing and the whole intended stay. Citizens of countries exempt from US visas can also qualify with a valid ESTA or a US entry in the past two years.
entries.note: The AVE page limits the AVE to ordinary-passport holders travelling for tourism who hold a current US visa in category B2, J, B1, O, P (P1-P2-P3), E or H-1B, valid through AVE processing and the intended stay; nationals of US visa-waiver jurisdictions can qualify with a US entry in the previous two years, a valid ESTA or one of those visas.

entries.old: Consular tourist visa required — BUT Chinese citizens who hold a valid US visa can enter without a visa or an AVE for tourism or business, for up to 30 days. They no longer apply for the AVE, and a Schengen visa does not qualify.
entries.new: Consular tourist visa required. Chinese ordinary-passport holders with a valid US visa of a similar category can instead enter without a consular visa or an AVE, as tourists or business travellers, for up to 30 days; the Migraciones AVE page adds that a US green card also qualifies, though Resolución 316/2025 names only the US visa. The stay can be extended once for a similar period, and a change of immigration category is not allowed.
entries.note: Resolución 316/2025 art. 1-2: ordinary passport, valid US visa of similar category, tourists and business people, up to 30 days, one extension of a similar period, no change of category. The Migraciones AVE page adds 'visa o green card de Estados Unidos'; the resolution names only the visa. The resolution does not mention Schengen visas, so that clause was dropped.

entries.old: Consular tourist visa required. Holders of a valid US visa can instead enter without a visa or an AVE, for tourism only and for up to 90 days. Indian citizens are no longer on the AVE list, and a Schengen visa does not qualify.
entries.new: Consular tourist visa required. Indian ordinary-passport holders with a valid US visa of a similar category can instead enter without a consular visa or an AVE, for tourism only and for up to 90 days; the US visa is checked with the relevant authorities. The stay can be extended once for a similar period, and a change of immigration category is not allowed. India is not on the AVE list.
entries.note: Resolución 353/2025 art. 1-2: ordinary passport, valid US visa of similar category verified with the relevant authorities, tourism only, up to 90 days, one extension of a similar period, no change of category.

entries.old: Consular tourist visa required, applied for at an Argentine embassy or consulate.
entries.new: Consular tourist visa required, applied for at an Argentine embassy or consulate. Dominican ordinary-passport holders with a valid US visa of a similar category can instead enter without a consular visa or an AVE, for tourism only and for up to 90 days. The stay can be extended once for a similar period, and a change of immigration category is not allowed.
entries.note: The row did not mention the waiver recorded in conditionalWaivers on 2026-09-25. Resolución 316/2025 art. 1: ordinary passport, valid US visa of similar category, tourism only, up to 90 days. The row now cites the Migraciones AVE page, which states the same.

entries.old: Chinese, Dominican and Indian citizens holding a valid US visa in a similar category can enter Argentina without a consular visa or an AVE. entries.new: visa-free with K-ETA: Botswana and Haiti 90 days, Bahrain, Guyana, Mauritius and Eswatini 30 days

The return-ticket rule was cited to the Foreign Ministry's consular services menu, which does not state it. The Interior Ministry's page "Entrada: requisitos y condiciones" states it: to return or transit, visitors must show a named, non-transferable, fixed-date ticket, and entry is refused without one.

entries.new: Cabo Delgado province, the Memba and Eráti districts of Nampula, and the Mecula and Marrupa districts of Niassa

entries.reason: The two-blank-pages rule was cited to the eVisa portal's front page, which does not state it. The FCDO's entry-requirements page does: "You need at least 2 blank pages for entry stamps."

The yellow fever rule was cited to the eVisa portal's front page, which does not state it. The FCDO's entry-requirements page does: a certificate is needed if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk.

Both were cited to the eVisa portal's front page, which states neither. The FCDO's entry-requirements page says that on arrival you may be asked to show proof of accommodation, a return or onward ticket and proof of enough money for your stay.

The 30-day extension was cited to the eVisa portal's front page, which does not state it. Global Affairs Canada's Mozambique page does: visitors may request one extension of 30 days from the immigration authorities.

entries.field: 14 passports not on the tourist eVisa list — entry requirement

entries.note: None of Andorra, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bahrain, Liechtenstein, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Oman, San Marino, Tajikistan, Tunisia, Turkmenistan or the UAE is among the 100 countries (plus Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macao) whose ordinary passport holders the Notice to Tourist says are eligible for the tourist visa.

entries.field: 12 passports on the tourist eVisa list — entry requirement

entries.note: The Notice to Tourist's exemption table gives Vietnam 30 days (Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, the Philippines and Thailand 14), for ordinary passports entering and leaving through Yangon, Mandalay or Naypyidaw international airports. The need-visa FAQ answer now says so.

entries.field: Singapore — ports for the visa exemption
entries.new: any international checkpoint
entries.note: The Notice to Tourist: from 1 September 2022 Singapore ordinary passport holders need no visa for tourist visits of up to 30 days and can enter and depart from all International Checkpoints.

entries.old: Yangon, Mandalay and Nay Pyi Taw airports only
entries.new: Yangon, Mandalay and Nay Pyi Taw international airports and the Kawthaung International Land Border Checkpoint
entries.note: The Notice to Tourist and the Notice to Business Traveller both list Kawthaung International Land Border Checkpoint as the fourth permitted port for eVisa holders. The summary, the land-borders tip and the overland-entry FAQ answer now name it.

entries.field: Tourist and business eVisa — processing time
entries.new: at least 3 working days
entries.note: Both notices say processing takes a minimum of 3 working days (Myanmar time), counted from the acknowledgement email sent after submission and payment. entries.reason: The passport table was cited to the eVisa front page, which does not list eligible nationalities. The Notice to Tourist lists the 100 eligible countries and the ASEAN exemptions, and is now the table's citation. The onward-ticket rule moves to it too: a proof of return ticket must be attached to the application.

The 6-months-on-arrival rule was cited to the eStay extension portal, which states six months' validity only as a condition for extending a business stay. The FCDO's entry-requirements page states the arrival rule: an expiry date at least 6 months after the day you arrive.

The yellow fever rule was cited to the eVisa front page, which does not state it. The FCDO's entry-requirements page does: a certificate is needed if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk.

entries.note: FCDO entry requirements: the passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after the date you arrive, and at least 3 blank pages. The passport-validity text now says three. Both move from the Ministry's front page, which states neither.

entries.new: multiple
entries.note: FCDO entry requirements: when granted a visa on arrival, you receive a multiple-entry visa valid for the period you requested. The fee is NAD 1,600 for travellers over 11, by either the arrival or the online route. Children aged 6 to 11 pay NAD 800 and under-6s pay nothing, which the fee note now says. The visa type moves from the Ministry's front page, which states none of it.

entries.reason: naurugov.nr no longer resolves. The government portal is now at nauru.gov.nr, and the FCDO links there too. It does not state the entry-requirement figures that cite it, so those stay marked portal-only and keep their dates.

The visa policy now cites the portal's Visa Requirements page. It says every visa application is made by email to Nauru Immigration, with a completed form and a passport copy. It does not state the 30-day stay or the flight and hotel bookings, so the date does not move.

The Immigration Division of the Department of Justice and Border Control lists the visa classes, the application forms and the visa fees under the Immigration Act 2014. It is now cited for both visa types.

entries.old: Approximately AUD 50, often collected on arrival
entries.new: AUD 50 for up to 1 month, AUD 150 for up to 2 months, AUD 250 for up to 3 months, paid with the application and non-refundable
entries.note: The Immigration Division's visitor visa fee table: $50 for up to 1 month, $150 for up to 2 months, $250 for up to 3 months. The Visitor's Visa form (Form 7) says the same under regulation 16 of the Immigration Regulations 2014. It adds that payment must go with the application (cash at the Nauru Revenue Office or a Nauruan consular post, or bank transfer) and is not refunded. The amount stays at 50. The FAQ and the cash tip no longer say the fee may be collected on arrival.

entries.new: at least 3 months after the date of arrival
entries.note: The FCDO: 'To enter Nauru, your passport must have an expiry date at least 3 months after the date you arrive.' Nauru's own Visitor's Visa form (justice.gov.nr) says the passport 'shall not be due to expire within 3 months from the date of your application'. Neither states a six-month rule. Moved off the government portal, which never stated it.

entries.reason: The Migración site still answers 403 behind a Cloudflare check, so nothing cited to it could be read. Three entry rules move to the FCDO's Nicaragua entry requirements page, which states each one. The passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after the date you arrive. A yellow fever certificate is needed if you are coming from a country with a risk of transmission. You may be refused entry without an onward ticket.

entries.old: 6 months on arrival; damaged passports frequently refused at the border
entries.new: 6 months on arrival
entries.note: The six-month rule is unchanged and now confirmed by the FCDO. No official page we could read says damaged passports are refused, so that sentence was removed.

entries.reason: The visa policy and both visa types were cited to the Foreign Ministry's front page, which does not state them. Its 'Entrée au Niger' page does. Every foreigner must show a passport with a Nigerien visa unless a bilateral or community agreement exempts them. The visa is applied for at a Nigerien embassy or consulate, and the fee is set by that post. At the point of entry a visa is granted only exceptionally, with the Interior Minister's authorization.

entries.new: 15 days
entries.note: 'Le délai de délivrance de visa est de 15 jours.'

entries.new: valid for the duration of the stay; no additional validity needed
entries.note: FCDO: 'Your passport should be valid for the proposed duration of your stay. No additional period of validity is needed.' The same page is now cited for the yellow fever certificate, which it states is required to enter Niger. The Foreign Ministry's front page stated neither.

entries.old: do-not-travel advisories from most Western governments ... Reconsider non-essential travel
entries.new: the FCDO advises against all travel to Niger; travel outside Niamey only with government permission and a security escort; gunfire near the Presidential Palace and airport on 29 August 2026
entries.note: The FCDO advises against all travel to Niger because of terrorist and criminal kidnappings of foreign nationals and a risk of terrorist attack throughout the country, including Niamey. It says the political situation remains unstable after the July 2023 coup. Foreign nationals may travel outside Niamey only with government permission and a Nigerien security and military escort. It reports gunfire near the Presidential Palace and Diori Hamani airport on 29 August. The old closing line 'Reconsider non-essential travel' was weaker than the advice. The level stays high-risk.

entries.old: required when arriving from a risk country
entries.new: required of all arriving travelers; infants 8 months or younger and adults 61 or older exempt
entries.note: FCDO: 'To enter Nigeria, you must have a certificate to prove you've had a yellow fever vaccination ... Infants aged 8 months or younger and adults aged 61 or older are exempt from this requirement.' The NIS front page we cited did not state it.

entries.old: 6 months on arrival, with a blank page for the entry stamp
entries.new: 6 months on arrival
entries.note: FCDO: 'your passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after the date you arrive.' The rule is unchanged and now cites this page instead of the NIS front page. No page we read states the blank page, so it stays only in blankPages, which still cites the portal.

entries.old: no link; 'airlines check the QR confirmation at check-in'
entries.new: links to lecard.immigration.gov.ng; free, required of all foreigners entering or leaving, refusal of entry or departure if not done
entries.note: The NIS Landing and Exit Card FAQ: all foreigners visiting or departing Nigeria must use the portal to pre-process arrival and departure. It is 'completely free', transit passengers are out of scope, and failure to comply 'shall lead to refusal of entry/departure at immigration checkpoints'. The NIS home page gives 1 May 2025 as the start date. No official page says airlines check the card at check-in, so that line was removed. Re-cited from the NIS front page.

entries.old: the north-east and north-west and some Middle Belt and riverine states are do-not-travel zones
entries.new: FCDO advises against all travel to Borno, Yobe, Adamawa, Gombe, Katsina and Zamfara and the Niger Delta riverine areas, and against all but essential travel to much of the rest of the north, the Middle Belt and parts of the south-east
entries.note: The FCDO's list of areas. The Middle Belt states (Niger, Kogi, Plateau, Taraba, Kwara, Benue) are 'all but essential', not 'all travel', and the old text called them do-not-travel zones. The level stays at exercise-caution.

entries.field: Safety assessment — what the cited advisory advises
entries.old: Foreign governments advise against all travel to North Korea
entries.new: The UK government advises against all but essential travel to North Korea
entries.note: The cited FCDO page (updated 10 December 2025, still current at 25 September 2026) says 'FCDO advises against all but essential travel to North Korea', not against all travel. The level stays high-risk: the page reports detentions of foreign nationals without access to their governments and severely limited consular support.

entries.reason: The currency rule was cited to the DPRK Foreign Ministry's front page, a Korean-language news page that does not state it. The FCDO's entry-requirements page states it: importing or exporting the won is illegal, and foreign currency is unrestricted but must be declared at customs. It also names the US dollar, the euro and Chinese yuan as the currencies accepted, and says credit cards are not.

entries.field: Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Azerbaijan, Armenia and Qatar — entry requirement
entries.new: visa required (Russia: exempt with an original tourist voucher for up to 30 days, or an original invitation for up to 90)
entries.note: The Foreign Ministry's country entries read 'Visa for foreign citizens: NEEDED' for all six. Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan exempt only diplomatic and official passports. The Russian entry cites the 2008 agreement on mutual travel (Official Gazette 119/2008): no visa for tourist trips of up to 30 days on an original voucher and the receiving tour operator's confirmation, or for visits of up to 90 days on an original invitation. The rows were cited to the Ministry's front page, which states none of this. The entries are current: the China entry mentions China's visa-free policy running to 31 December 2026, and the Taiwan entry a decision in force until 31 March 2030. We found no government decision that waives visas for these six.

entries.field: Mauritius, Seychelles, Nicaragua, Antigua and Barbuda, Bahamas, Barbados, El Salvador, Saint Kitts and Nevis and Taiwan — entry requirement
entries.new: visa-free (Taiwan: 90 days in any 180; the others: length of stay not stated)
entries.note: The Foreign Ministry's country entries read 'Visa for foreign citizens: NOT NEEDED' for all nine. The Taiwan entry adds 'for holders of Taiwanese passports containing the identity card number, for stay up to 90 days in any 180 days period. The Decision is in force until 31.03.2030'. The other eight entries give no length of stay, so maxStayDays is null rather than an assumed 90.

entries.field: Entry on a third-country visa or residence permit
entries.old: valid multiple-entry Schengen (type C) visa: up to 15 days per visit
entries.new: valid multiple-entry US, UK or Canadian visa (temporary decision, 1 January–31 December 2026), Schengen type C visa, or EU/Schengen residence: up to 15 days per entry, within 90 days in any 180
entries.note: The Ministry's page on visa requirements states the decision temporarily abolishing C visas for holders of a valid multiple-entry British, American or Canadian visa in their passport, for stays of up to 15 days, with the visa valid 5 days beyond the stay, 'valid from 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2026'. It states the same 15-day rule, within 90 days in any 180-day period, for Schengen type C visa holders and for third-country nationals with temporary or permanent residence in an EU or Schengen state.

entries.new: 70 EUR (35 EUR for children aged 6–12)

entries.reason: The C visa fee was cited to the Foreign Ministry's front page and hedged as 'commonly cited'. The Ministry's page on visa types states it: 'The fee pursuant to the LAF – Tariff No. 135 for short-stay and transit visa is – 60 euros or 35 euros for children aged 6-12'. The fee note now gives the children's rate and the tariff in place of the hedge.

The rule that visa applicants must show travel health insurance was cited to the front page. The Ministry's visa application procedure requires proof of valid travel medical insurance for the whole stay, and is now the citation.

The 48-hour police registration was cited to the Foreign Ministry's front page, which does not state it. The FCDO's entry-requirements page does: register with the local police within 48 hours of arrival. Hotels register you at check-in, and failing to register can lead to a fine, detention and a court hearing.

entries.new: more than NOK 25,000
entries.note: Norwegian Customs: 'If you are bringing currency with a value corresponding to more than NOK 25,000 to or from Norway, you must notify Norwegian Customs.' The penalty for not declaring is 20 per cent of the whole amount. The FCDO's Norway page still says '25,000 Norwegian krone or more'. We follow the customs authority.

entries.reason: The cash rule was cited to Norwegian Customs' English front page, which does not state it. Customs' page on currency states the threshold, the declaration form and the penalty.

The passport and onward-ticket rules were cited to UDI's front page, which answers 403 to our reader and does not state them anyway. The FCDO's Norway entry-requirements page states both: the passport must have been issued less than 10 years before arrival and expire at least 3 months after leaving the Schengen area, and at the border you may need to show a return or onward ticket and proof of accommodation.

entries.new: four weeks (28 days), extendable by one week

The page does not mention the six-month residence-permit condition in our text, so that condition is still unconfirmed.

entries.reason: The GCC-resident waiver was cited to the eVisa portal's front page, which does not state it. The portal's 'Know your Visa Type' page states it under 'Visit Unsponsored visas'.

The insurance and return-ticket rules for visa-free arrivals were cited to the eVisa portal's front page, which does not state them. The FCDO's Oman entry-requirements page does: visits of up to 14 days need no visa, and at border control you must show a return or onward ticket, proof of accommodation and proof of travel health insurance.

The passport rows were cited to the front page of the Pakistan Online Visa System, which states only that the system is open to citizens of 192 countries. The portal's Tourist Visa page states who is eligible (it links the list of countries eligible for a visit visa), that GCC citizens need no visa, the single-entry duration of up to 3 months and the processing times, and is now the default citation for the passport rows.

The Business eVisa was cited to the portal's front page, which states none of its terms. The portal's Business Visa page states the duration, the entries and the processing times, and is now the citation.

entries.field: Afghanistan, Libya, Palestine, Somalia, Syria and Yemen — entry requirement
entries.old: embassy visa (not eligible for the online visa)
entries.new: tourist eVisa, up to 90 days

entries.field: Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE — entry requirement
entries.new: visa-free (length of stay not stated)

entries.field: Business eVisa — validity, entries and processing

It does not state a stay per entry, so the 90-day stay is unchanged.

entries.field: Summary and "Do I need a visa?" answer
entries.old: around 175 nationalities online; the rest must apply at an embassy
entries.new: 192 countries on the eligibility list; GCC citizens need no visa
entries.note: Follows the two passport-row changes above.

entries.old: Arrival card and customs declaration handed out on the inbound flight, completed on the aircraft or on arrival

The Bureau of Customs and Border Protection's Immigration page says the same, and that the form generates a QR code shown at check-in and on arrival.

entries.reason: The passport, return-ticket and funds rules were cited to the National Immigration Service's home page, which states none of them. The Service's FAQ page lists the entry requirements: a passport valid for at least 3 months, proof of funds of no less than B/.500.00 (not required of children under 18), and a confirmed reservation to leave the country within the permitted period. It is now the citation for all three.

entries.new: other (at least 3 months)
entries.note: The FAQ page states "Presentar pasaporte o documento de viaje original, con un mínimo de 3 meses de vigencia." Our text already said the legal minimum is 3 months and that airlines often apply 6. Only the machine-readable rule changes, so a checklist no longer fails a passport with 3 to 6 months left. The text is unchanged.

entries.field: Fiji, Solomon Islands and Vanuatu — entry requirement
entries.new: visa on arrival, 30 days
entries.note: ICSA's Visa Information Guide says Melanesian Spearhead Group passport holders are eligible for a visa on arrival that is valid for stays of 30 days or less. ICSA's visa-on-arrival page lists all three countries, and the fee schedule sets the MSG visa fee at nil.

entries.field: Canada, UAE, Micronesia, Indonesia, Japan, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Nauru, Palau, Samoa, Singapore, Israel, Tonga, Tuvalu and the UK — entry requirement
entries.new: visa on arrival (the eVisa remains an option)
entries.note: ICSA's page says visa on arrival is currently available to citizens of all 15, and to French Polynesia, Wallis and Futuna, New Caledonia, the Cook Islands, Niue, Tokelau and the US Pacific territories. Mainland New Zealand, France and the United States are not eligible. China is listed for diplomatic, official and service passports only, so its row stays eVisa.

entries.new: 50 USD (no visa fee, plus the USD 50 eVisa fee)
entries.note: The Migration Service Fee schedule, linked as the current "Revised Migration Service Fees" from ICSA's fees page, sets a nil visa fee for the Easy Visitor Permit (30 or 60 days) and the other tourist classes, and a USD 50 eVisa fee. The 67 eVisa passport rows no longer call the eVisa free.

entries.new: 240 USD (USD 190 short-term single-entry visa fee plus the USD 50 eVisa fee)
entries.note: The same schedule lists the short-term multiple-entry business visa at USD 350.

entries.new: not extendable
entries.note: The fee schedule and the Visa Information Guide both say single-entry business visas and the Restricted Employment Visa are not extendable.

entries.new: 10 business days
entries.note: The Visa Information Guide says the turnaround for all visa applications is 10 working days if all requirements are met.

entries.old: paper arrival card and customs declaration issued on the inbound flight
entries.new: PNG Digital Arrival Card, online within 72 hours before arrival; mandatory before a boarding pass is issued; free
entries.note: ICSA's public notice of 6 August 2026 makes the PNGDAC a mandatory pre-arrival requirement for everyone, including PNG citizens and permanent residents, completed before boarding passes are issued. ICSA's PNGDAC page says it replaced the paper incoming passenger card from 1 October 2025 and is free, and the traveller guide gives the 72-hour window.

entries.reason: The passport, onward-ticket and proof-of-funds rules were cited to ICSA's home page, which does not state them. ICSA's Visa Information Guide does: passports valid at least 6 months from the date of travel, and a confirmed onward or return ticket and a guarantee of financial security for tourist and visiting-relative applicants.

The embassy tourist visa was cited to ICSA's home page. ICSA's Visitor Visa page states the usual single-entry 60-day stay from arrival and the paper application for travellers who are not eligible for a visa on arrival.

entries.field: Bahamas, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Trinidad and Tobago, United Arab Emirates and Philippines — entry requirement
entries.new: visa-free (length of stay not stated)
entries.note: The Foreign Ministry's list of nationalities that do not need a visa for Paraguay includes all five, with no restriction to diplomatic or official passports. The list gives no length of stay, so the rows leave it blank rather than assume 90 days.

entries.field: San Marino, Vatican City, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Thailand — entry requirement
entries.new: visa required (embassy)
entries.note: None of the six is on the Foreign Ministry's list of visa-exempt nationalities, and the page says any country not on the list needs a visa. Serbia is listed only for diplomatic, official and service passports, with ordinary passports needing a visa.

entries.old: avoid the northern departments of Concepción, San Pedro and Amambay
entries.new: take particular care in the departments bordering Brazil, including Concepción, San Pedro and Amambay
entries.note: The FCDO's regional-risks page says to take particular care in the departments bordering Brazil, where violent crime is rising, and that the EPP operates in northern San Pedro and southern Concepción. It does not advise against travel there. The level stays exercise-caution.

entries.reason: The passport rows were cited to the Foreign Ministry's home page, which does not list them. The Ministry's "Requisitos de Visa por Países" page lists the nationalities that do not need a visa and says every other nationality does, and is now the visa policy's citation. It does not state stay lengths.

entries.old: no mention of the Likouala border area
entries.new: the UK advises against all travel within 50 km of the border with the Central African Republic in Likouala
entries.note: FCDO advice, still current on 26 September 2026: it advises against all travel within 50 km of the Republic of Congo–Central African Republic border in Likouala Region. The Pool Region has had no live conflict reported since the 2017 ceasefire, and petty crime in Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire is unchanged. The level stays exercise-caution.

entries.field: Safety — drones from the war in Ukraine
entries.new: drones from the war in neighboring Ukraine have crossed into Romanian airspace and some carrying explosives have landed or washed ashore; follow RO-Alert warnings and do not approach military debris
entries.note: FCDO update of 18 September 2026, still current on 26 September. The rest of the text, on petty theft in Bucharest, taxi overcharging and stray dogs, matches the advice, and the level stays generally-safe.

entries.field: Barbados, Bhutan, Eswatini, Iceland, Jordan, Kenya, Papua New Guinea, Saint Lucia, Tonga, Trinidad and Tobago, Turkmenistan and Zimbabwe — entry requirement
entries.old: visa from a Russian consulate; not eligible for the unified e-visa
entries.new: unified e-visa, stay of up to 30 days
entries.note: All twelve are on the list of countries whose citizens are eligible for the unified e-visa, which the portal's front page carries (65 countries). Whether any of them also has a visa-free bilateral arrangement was not checked.

entries.old: at least 6 months beyond the visa's expiry
entries.new: at least 6 months from the date the application is submitted
entries.note: The portal: "Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months from the date of submitting the application for a unified e-visa." The general rule for consular visas and the two blank pages are not stated on this page.

entries.field: Unified e-visa: validity and stay in the tip and FAQ answers
entries.old: valid 60 days, stay of up to 16 days
entries.new: valid 120 days, stay of up to 30 days
entries.note: The 29 August change updated the visa type and the passport rows but left the tip and two FAQ answers on the old figures. The portal states 120 days from issue and 30 days from entry.

entries.field: Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA) for every foreign visitor
entries.old: visa-free, nothing to obtain before travel
entries.new: eTA required before travel: USD 17 single entry, usually processed within 24 hours, valid 90 days from issue
entries.note: The Ministry of National Security's Electronic Border Management System, linked from gov.kn and mofa.gov.kn: "The eTA is mandatory for all foreign visitors"; it must be shown at check-in and boarding. Day-trip cruise passengers and air passengers transiting without leaving the airport are exempt. The 85 visa-free rows keep their 90-day stay and now read eta. The 12 CARICOM rows keep free movement, and their notes now say the eTA still applies. The page also says there are no vaccination requirements, which conflicts with the yellow-fever entry; that entry is unchanged.

entries.field: Andorra, Namibia, Samoa and Haiti — entry requirement
entries.old: visa-free (Andorra, Namibia, Samoa); CARICOM free movement (Haiti)
entries.new: visa required, applied for online
entries.note: All four are on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' list of 67 countries and territories whose nationals require a visa for entry.

entries.old: from a Kittitian mission or honorary consulate; no eVisa
entries.new: online, through the Ministry of National Security's e-visa platform
entries.note: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs: "Travelers who currently require a visa to enter the federation may apply online." The link goes to the Ministry of National Security's e-visa platform. The 101 rows that need a visa now read evisa. 65 of them are on the ministry's visa-required list. The other 36 are not on it, and they keep the visa requirement until a reviewer confirms their status. The summary and the need-visa FAQ answer now say the same.

entries.reason: The visa-policy rows were cited to the government's home page, which does not state them. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs' list of visa-required countries does, and is now the default citation.

The visitor and business visas were cited to the government's home page. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs' Passport and Visa Services page states that a visa is applied for online, and is now their citation. It does not state the processing time, validity or stay.

entries.field: Visitor and business visa: fee and processing time
entries.new: GBP 35 (holiday), GBP 40 (business); 3–5 working days
entries.note: The government portal's Visas service entry, for the High Commission for Saint Lucia (London): "Processing Time: 3 to 5 working days", "Fee: GBP35.00 (holiday); GBP40.00 (business); GBP30.00 (student)". The fee notes say other missions set their own fees. The page does not state validity or length of stay.

entries.field: Visa-free entry for holders of Schengen, EU, UK or US visas
entries.old: Holders of a valid Schengen, US or UK visa — or a residence permit issued by one of those countries — can enter Serbia visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, regardless of nationality. The stay cannot exceed the validity of the visa you are traveling on.
entries.new: Holders of a valid Schengen, EU member state, UK or US visa — or a residence permit issued by a Schengen country, an EU member state or the US — can enter Serbia visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, regardless of nationality. The stay cannot exceed the validity of the visa or residence permit you are traveling on.
entries.note: The Government Decision of 30 October 2014, as the MFA states it, covers a valid 'Schengen, UK and EU Member States' visa, or visa of the United States' and a 'residence permit in the countries of the Schengen area, EU or the United States'. A UK residence permit is not on the list; EU member-state visas are.

entries.old: at least 90 days beyond intended entry
entries.new: at least 90 days after the intended date of departure
entries.note: MFA general visa requirements: 'passport must be valid at least 90 days after the intended date of departure from the Republic of Serbia, with at least two consecutive blank pages, and issued within the past 10 years'. The FCDO says the same for British visitors.

entries.old: not required; about EUR 50 a day 'commonly cited'
entries.new: required; EUR 50 per day
entries.note: MFA General Entry Requirements list 'Proof of sufficient funds for staying in Serbia. Sufficient funds are considered to be 50 Euros per day of stay, proved by possession of the appropriate amount of cash, bank statement', and entry 'shall be denied' to a foreigner without them (Law on Foreigners).

entries.new: more than €10,000
entries.note: FCDO: declare cash or travellers cheques 'worth more than 10,000 euros'. Serbia's Customs Administration says the same ('if it is more than EUR 10.000 ... your duty is to declare it'), but carina.rs is not on the official-hosts list, so the FCDO page is cited.

entries.note: Follows the Kuwait, Oman, Qatar and Saudi Arabia rows, which the MFA now lists as 'Visas required' for ordinary passports; the UAE and Bahrain remain visa-free for 90 days.

entries.reason: The passport rows cited the Foreign Ministry's home page, which states no visa rule. Its 'Visa regime' directory links one page per country with the rule for diplomatic, official and ordinary passports; all 194 were read on 26 September 2026 and every row compared. Rows that changed cite their own country page.

The visa-waiver for Schengen/EU/UK/US visa holders, the C and D visa types and the passport rule cited the ministry's home page. The ministry's Visa Requirements page states them: the 2014 Government Decision, C visas for up to 90 days in 180, D visas for 90 to 180 days, and the passport rule for applicants. It also says visas can be applied for online at welcometoserbia.gov.rs and that Serbia has issued Digital Travel Authorizations since 23 April 2025.

The onward-ticket and funds rules cited the ministry's home page. Its General Entry Requirements page states them: border authorities 'may ask to produce ... a return flight ticket, a proof of paid hotel booking', and EUR 50 a day in funds.

Police registration and the cash declaration cited the ministry's home page, which states neither. The FCDO's Serbia entry requirements do: register with the local police within 24 hours (hotels do it automatically), and declare cash over EUR 10,000.

entries.old: Cash above roughly SCR 50,000 (or the foreign-currency equivalent) should be declared on arrival. Confirm current thresholds with Seychelles customs before traveling with large amounts.
entries.new: Cash of SCR 50,000 or more (or the foreign-currency equivalent) must be declared to Customs on arrival and on departure.
entries.note: The Seychelles Revenue Commission's passenger guide: 'any person (visitors/residents) who physically transports cash in an aggregate sum of SCR50, 000 (or equivalent in foreign currency) or more, shall make a declaration to the Customs Division upon entering and exiting the Seychelles' (Cross Border Declaration Regulations, S.I. 11 of 2022). The threshold is exact, not approximate, and applies on departure too.

entries.reason: The passport rows, the visitor's permit extension and the onward-ticket rule cited the travel authorisation portal's front page, which states none of them. The Immigration and Civil Status page on the Visitor's Permit does: all visitors need a Travel Authorisation before departure; the permit is issued on arrival for up to three months, extendable by three-month periods to twelve months at SCR 5,000 per extension; and a valid return or onward ticket, confirmed accommodation and sufficient funds are conditions of the permit.

The yellow fever rule cited the portal's front page, which does not state it. The portal's FAQ does: a certificate only when travelling from an endemic country, none for a transit of under 12 hours, and none for travellers aged 60 or over. The answer sits in a collapsed accordion, so it is not in the page's default rendered text.
The passport rule cited the portal's front page, which does not state it. The FCDO's Seychelles entry requirements do: 'your passport must be valid for the duration of your stay'.

The MFA eVisa portal was marked portal-only. It renders client-side, and its application form loads the country dictionary from its own API (e-visa.gov.uz:8443/api/v1/dic/countries/en), read on 26 September 2026. The dictionary lists 136 nationalities with a status code. Selecting a nationality in the form shows what each code means: 1 = 'Visa for 30 days. processing time 3 WORKING DAYS' (44 nationalities); 2 = 'Visa-free entry for up to 30 days.' (82); 3 = 'Visa-free entry for up to 60 days.' (Kyrgyzstan); 4 = 'Visa-free entry procedure.' (Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, France, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Moldova, Russia, Ukraine). The portal's terms say the eVisa is issued only to the countries with a simplified procedure. They state the fees as USD 20 single, 35 double and 50 multiple entry, a decision within 2 working days, a stay of up to 30 days and 90 days' validity. Every passport row was compared, the portal-only flag is cleared, and the 83 rows that differed are logged separately.

entries.field: FAQ — do I need a visa
entries.old: Andorra issues no visas at all. Entry is governed by Schengen rules because you must pass through France or Spain. EU/EEA citizens and Schengen visa-free nationalities (US, UK, Japan and many more) just drive in; if your passport needs a Schengen visa, get a multiple-entry one so you can re-enter France or Spain afterward.

entries.note: Stated for British (FCDO), Canadian (travel.gc.ca: 'the visa must be obtained at an Iraqi Embassy or Consulate or online before travelling') and Australian (Smartraveller: 'you must apply online at the e-Visa Portal to obtain an electronic visa before you travel to Iraq') passports; those three rows now cite their own government's page. The other 37 follow the FCDO's statement that visa on arrival has ended; no nationality-specific official confirmation was found for them.

entries.old: Kurdistan issues its own entry stamps at Erbil and Sulaymaniyah airports to a broader list of nationalities
entries.new: KRG e-Visa (visit.gov.krd), online or on arrival for its Country List A, sponsor needed for others; IQD 100,000; valid 90 days from issue; 30-day stay; valid in the Kurdistan Region only
entries.note: FCDO: 'The government of the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI) has introduced a new e-visa process… It is also possible to obtain a visa on arrival. Both types of visas are valid for travel in KRI only.' Smartraveller says the same. Fee, validity and stay are from the KRG portal FAQ (visit.gov.krd/faq), read today; that host is not yet in data/official-hosts.json so it is not cited as a source. Canada says a Kurdistan e-Visa must be obtained online before travelling.

entries.reason: The visa regime was cited to the MFA consular department's landing page, which states no list. The MFA embassy network's Visas page (modified 14 Nov 2025) publishes the list of states whose nationals need no short-stay visa (short stay: under 3 months): 104 entries. It states no stay length beyond that and nothing about holders of Schengen, US or UK visas, so the 15-day waiver keeps its old citation. Slovenia is absent from the list; its row keeps the old citation pending review.

entries.new: visa-free, short stays (up to 90 days)
entries.note: All 52 appear on the MFA's 'Lista e shteteve që nuk kanë nevojë për viza' (Brazil, Argentina, Mexico, Israel, Malaysia, Singapore, most of Central America and the Caribbean, Pacific and southern African states among them).

entries.new: embassy visa
entries.note: Bosnia and Herzegovina is not on the MFA's visa-free list, which names Kosovo's other regional neighbours (Albania, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia).

entries.field: Summary and 'Do I need a visa?'
entries.old: EU/Schengen, a broad Western list and Balkan neighbours visa-free
entries.new: adds most of Latin America and the Caribbean, the Gulf, Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, Israel and the Pacific; Bosnia and Herzegovina needs a visa

entries.old: Kuwait admits GCC nationals freely and issues eVisas and visas on arrival to citizens of around 50 countries — including the US, UK, EU member states and much of East Asia — for tourist stays of up to three months; everyone else needs a sponsored visit visa arranged in advance.
entries.new: Kuwait admits GCC nationals freely and issues eVisas and visas on arrival to citizens of around 50 countries — including the US, UK, EU member states and much of East Asia — for tourist stays of up to three months. Most other nationalities can apply for the eVisa online if they hold a valid US, UK or Schengen visa; otherwise they need a sponsored visit visa arranged in advance.
entries.note: The Kuwait Visa platform's nationality checker, read today, answers 'You are eligible for applying online e-visa' for other nationalities holding a valid US, UK or Schengen tourist visa, and asks residence-permit holders for their occupation (the us-visa conditional waiver). The prose said every other nationality needs a sponsor, which that route contradicts.

entries.field: FAQ — do I need a visa
entries.old: GCC nationals enter freely without a visa. Citizens of around 50 countries — including the US, UK, EU member states, Canada, Australia, Japan and South Korea — can obtain a KWD 3 eVisa online or a visa on arrival at Kuwait International Airport. All other nationalities need a visit visa arranged in advance through a sponsor in Kuwait or a Kuwaiti embassy.
entries.new: GCC nationals enter freely without a visa. Citizens of around 50 countries — including the US, UK, EU member states, Canada, Australia, Japan and South Korea — can obtain a KWD 3 eVisa online or a visa on arrival at Kuwait International Airport. Most other nationalities can apply for the eVisa online if they hold a valid US, UK or Schengen tourist visa; a US, UK, Schengen or GCC residence permit may also qualify, depending on occupation. Everyone else needs a visit visa arranged in advance through a sponsor in Kuwait or a Kuwaiti embassy.
entries.note: The Kuwait Visa platform's nationality checker, read today, answers 'You are eligible for applying online e-visa' for other nationalities holding a valid US, UK or Schengen tourist visa, and asks residence-permit holders for their occupation (the us-visa conditional waiver). The prose said every other nationality needs a sponsor, which that route contradicts.

entries.field: Declaration: Health declaration form and screening (Ebola measures)
entries.new: mandatory health declaration and screening on arrival (Ebola measures)
entries.note: FCDO: 'all travellers must complete a health declaration form, declare any travel through an affected country in the previous 21 days, and undergo health screening on arrival'. No Malagasy official page read states it.

entries.new: mandatory Traveller Health Check form (on arrival via QR code or in advance)
entries.note: FCDO: 'The Ministry of Health and Sanitation require arriving passengers to complete a Traveller Health Check form. This can be accessed on arrival through a QR code or completed in advance.' The Ministry's form at poe.health.gov.mw/self-screen loads and allows declaring up to 2 days ahead.

entries.field: Visitor visa issued in advance — fee
entries.new: USD 100, non-refundable
entries.note: The RMI Embassy in Washington: 'Citizens from ALL OTHER countries not listed in A or B above must apply for visa PRIOR TO traveling to the Republic. Visitors Visa (V-1) requires a non-refundable application processing fee of $100.00 USD.' The visa type now cites the embassy. Its processing time, 90-day validity and 30-day stay are not stated there and are unchanged.

entries.old: not required — No published minimum. Officers may ask visitors to show they can support themselves; carrying US dollars in cash is the practical answer, since card acceptance is patchy.
entries.new: required of all visitors; no amount published
entries.note: 'All visitors traveling to the Marshall Islands must have a valid passport at least 6 months, must have sufficient funds for stay, and have an onward/return air or sea ticket.' Previously cited to the FCDO page, which does not state it.

entries.new: https://safemauritius.govmu.org/
entries.note: safemauritius.govmu.org is the Ministry of Health and Wellness's 'Mauritius All-in-One Travel Digital Form'. It states: 'Travellers are required, under Mauritian law, to complete the Health Declaration Form before travelling to Mauritius. Proof of completion of the form will be required at boarding.' and that it is 'completely free of charge'. The host is now registered, so the declaration links to it.

entries.reason: The national government portal states none of the visa rules. The FSM visitor site's Regulations page, linked from gov.fm and signed by the Chief of the Division of Immigration & Labor, states them: no permit for visits of 30 days or less, extensions of up to 60 days, one-year entry permits for US, Palauan and Marshallese citizens, and the onward-ticket rule. The visa policy, the extension and the onward ticket now cite it.

entries.new: 60 days
entries.note: 'A permit is not required for a person visiting the FSM for 30 days or less.' 'All other noncitizens may be issued an entry permit for an additional period not to exceed 60 days.' Applied to the 195 visa-free rows and the extension.

entries.field: US, Marshall Islands and Palau — length of stay
entries.new: entry permit for the visit, up to one year; birth certificate accepted as proof of citizenship
entries.note: 'Citizens and nationals of the Republic of Palau, the Republic of the Marshall Islands and the United States may be issued an entry permit for the duration of the visit which shall not exceed one year.' 'Citizens and nationals of the FSM, Republic of Palau, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, or the United States may prove citizenship or nationality by possessing a passport, birth certificate or FSM entry permit.' The US note no longer says a passport is required.

entries.field: FAQ — the Compact for US citizens
entries.old: Under the Compact, US citizens may enter the Federated States of Micronesia without a visa and may live and work there indefinitely, and FSM citizens have the same right in the United States. You still pass through immigration and need a valid passport, and local rules on employment and land ownership apply.
entries.new: no visa; passport or birth certificate; entry permit up to one year
entries.note: Matches the US row changed above.

entries.reason: The bilateral visa waivers were cited to the eVisa portal, which gives no stay lengths. The MFA Consular Department's list of countries whose citizens travel to Mongolia visa-free gives, per country, the passport types, the days allowed and the date in force; 30 ordinary-passport rows, plus Cuba and Serbia, now cite it. It also lists the 34 countries exempted for tourism (30 days) for 2023–2026, matching our rows. Russia and Ukraine keep their old citation (see review notes).

entries.field: UAE, Colombia, Dominican Republic — entry regime
entries.new: visa-free: UAE 30 days (since 2023), Colombia 90 days on ordinary passports (since 26 Jan 2026), Dominican Republic 90 days (since 10 Jun 2026)
Ecuador, Peru, Paraguay 90 days; Maldives, Uruguay, Uzbekistan, Vietnam 30 days
eVisa; visa-free only on diplomatic and official passports
entries.note: The MFA lists Cuba (30 days, 2001) and Serbia (90 days, 30 Jan 2026) only under diplomatic and official passports.

entries.new: tourism only, 1 June 2022 to 31 December 2026

entries.field: Germany and Canada — basis of the 30-day waiver
entries.new: standing bilateral waivers (Germany since 2013, Canada since 2014); neither is on the 2026 exemption list
certificate required if arriving from a polio-affected country
entries.note: FCDO: 'To enter Morocco, you must have a certificate to prove you’ve had a polio vaccine if you’re coming from a polio-affected country.'

entries.new: certificate required if arriving from a polio-affected country
entries.note: FCDO: 'a polio vaccine, if you’re coming from certain countries with a transmission risk'.

entries.field: Visa types: Tourist eVisa / ETA (15, 30, 90 days)
entries.new: eVisa/ETA bought online before travel: 30 USD/15 days, 50 USD/30 days, 125 USD/90 days, multiple entry
entries.note: Department of Immigration: 'Apply directly to the Department of Immigration Nepal for an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) / eVisa … Pay in USD online via card · Approved visa sent by email · Tourist visa: 15, 30, or 90 days'; fees 'USD 30 / 50 / 125'; 'Use your visa within 6 months from the date of issue.' Added alongside visa on arrival for the 185 passports that get it; not for the 12 nationalities the page says must apply via an embassy.

entries.new: mandatory only for travellers from Ebola-affected countries (NCDC); others exempt at this time
entries.note: NCDC portal (26 Sep 2026): 'Travellers from countries with active or relevant Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) transmission may be required to complete a health declaration form before boarding. Passengers from all other countries are exempt at this time.' FCDO instead says 'You must fill in an online Nigeria Health Declaration Form before entering Nigeria. This includes transit passengers.' Modelled as not mandatory per the operator; conflict flagged for review.

entries.reason: The government portal states none of the visa rules. The Bureau of Customs and Border Protection's Immigration page states them: the visa-waiver agreements, the tourist visa on arrival and its extensions, the six-month passport rule, the onward ticket, proof of support and the USD 100 environmental fee. The visa policy, both visa types, passport validity, onward ticket, proof of funds and the environmental fee now cite it.

entries.path: visaPolicy.byPassport (AT, BE, BG, HR, CZ, DK, EE, FI, FR, DE, GR, HU, IS, IT, LV, LI, LT, LU, MT, NL, NO, PL, PT, RO, SK, SI, ES, SE, CH)
entries.new: visa-free, 90 days in any 180-day period
entries.note: 'Palau signed a mutual visa-waiver agreement with the European Union on 7 December 2015. This agreement allows all citizens of states that are contracting parties to the Schengen Agreement to stay without a visa for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period.' Applied to the 29 Schengen states. Cyprus and Ireland are not Schengen states and keep the visa-on-arrival row.

entries.new: visa-free, 30 days
entries.note: 'Palau signed a mutual visa-waiver agreement with the Russia on 28 September 2018 which entered into force on 27 December 2018. This agreement allows citizens of Russia to stay without a visa for a period of 30 days.'

entries.new: visa-free (length of stay not stated)
entries.note: 'Effective, December 01, 2018, Palauan and Taiwanese nationals seeking visa-free entry into Taiwan and Palau respectively must hold an ordinary, official or diplomatic passport valid for at least 6 months; not intend to work, study or reside ... and hold a return flight ticket.' The page gives no stay length, so the row publishes none.

entries.new: visa before travel, 30 days
entries.note: 'The application process is different for nationals of Bangladesh and Myanmar, as they need to apply for the visa before they reach Palau, from their country of residence. Nationals of these two countries should contact the Palau diplomatic mission in their country, other representative authorities or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.'

entries.new: 60 days (two 30-day extensions)
entries.note: 'The tourist visa for Palau is valid for a period of 30 days and may be extended for two additional 30-day periods.' Applied to the 162 visa-on-arrival rows, the two visa-before-travel rows and the visa type.

entries.old: Approximate — commonly quoted around USD 50 for each additional 30 days
entries.new: USD 50 renewal fee; apply at least seven days before expiry
entries.note: 'You must apply at least seven days before the expiration date of your current visa at the Division of Immigration.' 'The fee is $50 USD for renewal.' The amount stays at 50; it is no longer described as approximate.

entries.old: not required — No published amount. Immigration officers may ask where you are staying and how you will support yourself. Have your hotel booking to hand.
entries.new: required of all visitors; no amount published
entries.note: 'All visitors, entering the Republic must provide proof that the visitor has sufficient support during the length of the visit and shall not become a public charge. Proof of such support may be in the form of a letter of credit, or other evidence as may be acceptable to the Director. Adequate support shall be determined on a case-by-case basis by the Director.'

entries.old: Yes. The Bureau of Immigration in Koror can extend the entry permit, generally in 30-day blocks for a fee of around USD 50 each. Apply before your current permit expires and bring your passport and onward ticket.
entries.new: Schengen 90 days visa-free, Russia 30, Bangladesh and Myanmar visa before travel; two 30-day extensions at USD 50 each, applied for seven days before expiry
entries.note: The summary and FAQ now match the rows and visa types changed above.

entries.new: required from all arrivals
entries.note: FCDO: 'To pass border control in the Republic of Congo, you must have certificates to prove you’ve had … a polio vaccine, due to the risk of polio transmission.'

entries.new: 1–7 business days
entries.note: The SMF e-visa portal: 'Terá uma resposta ao seu pedido num período de 7 dias úteis. nº2 do artigo 20 do Decreto Lei 11/2009.' The same page says 'O pagamento será feito na fronteira!' (payment is made at the border) and states no amount; the source's not-stated mark is cleared. The page does not state the 90-day validity, 30-day stay or extension, which stand unconfirmed.

entries.old: Approximate. The Migration and Border Service's e-visa portal does not show the fee; it says payment is made at the border.
entries.new: Not a published visa fee. The Migration and Border Service's e-visa portal does not show one and says payment is made at the border. The FCDO says every arrival pays a €20 entry fee on arrival, payable in euros, US dollars or dobras.
entries.note: FCDO Border control: 'You must pay a 20-euro entry fee when you arrive in the country. You can also pay in US dollars or local currency.' It is stated as an entry fee for every arrival, not as the eVisa fee, so the note no longer calls €20 the visa fee. The amount field still reads €20; a levies entry may be the better model (left for review).

entries.old: 6-months-on-arrival — Your passport should be valid for at least 6 months on arrival, with a blank page for the entry stamp.
entries.new: other — eVisa applicants upload a passport valid for at least three months beyond the last day of stay the visa allows. The FCDO tells visa-free British visitors only that the passport must be valid for the whole stay.
entries.note: SMF e-visa portal: 'Passaporte digitalizado em arquivo pdf com validade de três meses superior a data limite de permanência indicada no visto (Al.c 1 Artº 13 Decreto Lei 11/2009)'. The FCDO: 'Your passport must be valid for the duration of your stay.' No official page read states six months on arrival.

entries.old: all — Visitors are expected to hold a return or onward ticket, and airlines routinely check it before boarding flights to the islands.
entries.new: visa-applicants — eVisa applicants must attach a return ticket to the application.
entries.note: SMF e-visa portal: 'É obrigatório anexar o Bilhete de Passagem IDA / Volta'. It states this for eVisa applicants; no official page read states it for visa-free arrivals.

entries.old: not required, no amount — No fixed amount is published; immigration officers may ask visitors to show means of support and an accommodation address.
entries.new: required of visa applicants, €100 per day — eVisa holders must show proof of means of subsistence of €100 per day at the border.
entries.note: SMF e-visa portal, 'Informações adicionais na Fronteira': 'Apresentação do comprovativo do meio de subsistência 100€/diario'.

entries.reason: The insurance rule cited the eVisa portal's front page, which does not state it. Visit Saudi's visa-regulations FAQ does, under 'Do I need the medical insurance to apply for tourist visa?': 'A health insurance policy ... is issued along with your eVisa and its cost is included within the eVisa fee. Medical insurance coverage is valid for one year from the date of issue.' GCC residents 'obtain the medical insurance as a part of the tourist visa application process.' The FAQ does not restate the rule for visa-on-arrival visitors; the text is unchanged.

EUR-Lex records it in force: provisionally applied from 21 November 2015, entered into force 1 December 2016, no end of validity. Germany's Federal Foreign Office agrees with the agreement: German citizens need no visa for stays of up to 90 days per half-year, with a return or onward ticket and sufficient funds. The 2026-09-01 pass had settled these rows on Tonga's list. Ireland is outside the agreement (Article 2) and keeps its visa on arrival from Tonga's list.

The treaty ranks above the ministry list. Resolved by hierarchy. The six months previously published matched neither source.

entries.old: Foreign Ministry advisory cited; prior approval unsourced

The authority running the procedure ranks above the ministry. Resolved by hierarchy.
