entries.old: single-entry visa, 90-day stay; British row with no stay
entries.new: single-entry visa 30 days (USD 30); multiple-entry 90 days (USD 60) named in the fee note; British row 30 days
entries.note: The Honduran Embassy in London's visa page (hondurasembassyuk.com/visa, linked from the FCDO) prices 'Visa Sencilla (30 días): $30.00' and 'Visa Múltiple (90 días): $60.00', and says tourists may stay at most 90 days, extendable by 90 at the INM. The FCDO (read today) says British visitors get 'a 30-day visit entry stamp'. The two agree once single and multiple visas are told apart, so this is not a conflict. The embassy's .com host is not yet in data/official-hosts.json, so the visa type keeps its INM citation (portal, not stating the figure) until it is registered.

entries.field: Passport validity — two statements on the e-Visa page
entries.old: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months from the date of arrival and have at least 2 blank pages. (cited to the UK Foreign Office)
entries.new: 6 months from arrival and 2 blank pages kept, now cited to the e-Visa page; the 'at application' wording noted in the text
entries.note: India's e-Visa page (read today) says the passport should have at least six months' validity 'at the time of making application', while its FAQ (Q12) says 'at-least for next 06 (six) months from the date of arrival'. The UK Foreign Office also counts from arrival and agrees with the published rule, so it is not the losing side. Same source, same rank, no date for either passage: the stricter reading wins (stricter).

entries.field: e-Medical Visa — validity, stay and extension
entries.old: validity 120 days, stay 60 days, extendable by 60 days
entries.new: valid one year (365 days) from arrival, multiple entry; no stated stay cap; not extendable
entries.note: The e-Visa page's visa-type listing (read today) gives e-Medical Visa (e-M1 V) 'Duration: One year (365 days) from the date of arrival into India. Entries: Multiple'. Its FAQ (Q9) still says 60 days from first arrival — in an answer that also describes the e-Conference visa, a category the listing has since folded into e-Business (e-B5 V), so the FAQ is the older text and loses (newer). The page says every e-Visa is non-extendable and non-convertible (instructions and FAQ Q10).

entries.old: USD 26 (approximate; cited to the ETA-IL site, which does not state it)
entries.new: USD 32 (€28) at Israeli missions; 105 NIS through the eVisa-B2 pilot
entries.note: Not a conflict: two channels, two fees. The Foreign Ministry's consular tariff (gov.il, filtered to 'B/2-Visitor Visa', updated for 2026, read today) sets USD 32 / €28 at every mission shown. The Population and Immigration Authority's eVisa-B2 page (israel-entry.piba.gov.il/learn-about-evisa-b2, read today) charges a 105 NIS non-refundable handling fee for the online pilot open to Indian and Sri Lankan passport holders resident there. PIBA's in-country service page (gov.il/en/service/request_for_tourist_visa_b2, last updated 1 January 2024) lists 100 NIS for invitation applications made in Israel. No official page states USD 26.

entries.field: Bulgaria, Croatia and Romania — entry requirement
entries.new: visitor's visa, unless a tourist for 30 days or less holding a valid US, Canadian, UK or Schengen visa with proof of measles, rubella and polio vaccination (added to the us-visa waiver)
entries.note: PICA's table (Visa Unit, last updated 19 July 2023), read today, for all three: 'NO visa required for 30 days or less as tourists (Effective September 22, 2014) providing they have a USA, Canada, UK or Schengen Visa & possess proof of vaccination against Measles, Rubella & Polio'. No official source states the 90 days; these three rows were missed in the 26 September pass, so this is a correction, not a conflict.

entries.old: CARICOM free movement, 180 days (no own citation)
entries.new: 180 days kept; PICA's "90 days" and the CARICOM decision named in the row's notes (caricom.org is not a registered official host, so the decision cannot be linked yet)
entries.note: PICA's table lists 'SURINAME NO visa required for 90 days'. The Conference of Heads of Government decided that CARICOM nationals travelling to other Member States be granted a definite entry of six months (reported in the communiqué of the 19th Inter-Sessional Meeting, Nassau, March 2008, on caricom.org). A decision of the Community's supreme organ ranks above a national immigration table. Resolved by hierarchy.

entries.old: extendable by 60 days, to a total of about 3 months
entries.new: extendable for up to 6 months from the date of entry
entries.note: Not a conflict: no official source stated the 3-month total. The Ministry of Interior's service page for extending a temporary stay (read today) lets a foreign visitor extend 'for a period not exceeding 6 months from the date of entry', and the UK Foreign Office says the visit visa can be extended online for up to 6 months. 27 rows' extendableDays and the visa type moved from 60 to 150 days; 130 row notes and two FAQ answers reworded.

entries.new: prior approval kept, cited to the Ministry of Interior; its list without Syria shown beside it
entries.note: The Ministry's restricted-nationalities list (read today, EN and AR) does not name Syria. The Ministry's news item 'new facilitation for Syrian investors and business people' (23 July, among the July 2026 items) exempts chamber-of-commerce card holders and their families from the prior approval, which it treats as the rule for other Syrians. Same authority, and the list carries no date of its own (only the site-wide footer), so the version that cannot strand a traveller wins (stricter).

entries.new: prior approval kept with the Ministry's exemptions, cited to its FAQ; its October 2024 decision shown beside it
entries.note: The Ministry of Interior announced on 27 October 2024 that Libyan nationals may enter without prior approval, and Libya is not on its restricted list. Its FAQ (read today) still says Libyan and Yemeni nationals need prior approval unless they hold qualifying residence, a Schengen or US visa, or come for treatment. Same authority; the FAQ is undated, so the stricter version wins (stricter). Flagged for review: the dated decision is probably the newer statement.

entries.field: Palestine and South Sudan — entry requirement
entries.old: Prior approval from the Jordanian Ministry of Interior is generally required. Apply through a Jordanian embassy or an approved tour operator well before travel.
entries.new: visa on arrival, 30 days, extendable to 6 months from entry
entries.note: Not a conflict: the prior-approval note had no official source. The Ministry of Interior's list of restricted nationalities (English and Arabic, read today) defines restricted countries as those that need prior approval and names neither Palestine nor South Sudan (it lists the Republic of the Sudan). The FAQ's prior-approval groups do not name them either.

entries.new: 90 days in any 12 months (the Visa Exemption Order); the UK advice's one month on arrival kept in the note
entries.note: Kiribati's Immigration Entry and Visa Exemption Order 2023, para. 3.3 (read today by OCR of the gazetted scan), says the maximum stay under the exemption 'must not exceed 90 days in any given 12 month period'. The UK Foreign Office says visitors can come without a visa for up to one month, are normally granted a one-month stay and may extend in one-month steps. The order is law and outranks another government's advice: resolved by hierarchy. 120 rows have no source of their own, so the FCDO's statement is recorded in their notes; summary and two FAQ answers reworded.

entries.old: A yellow fever certificate is required from travelers aged 1 and over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. Almost no routing to Kiribati passes through such a country, so in practice this affects very few visitors.
entries.new: no vaccination requirement
entries.note: WHO's International Travel and Health Annex 1 (18 November 2022, revised 3 January 2023, read today) lists every country requiring proof of yellow fever vaccination, and Kiribati is not on it. The fact cited the Ministry's home page, which does not state it (marked not-stated on 26 September); the Immigration Procedures 2020, the Visa Exemption Order and the Kiribati Tourism entry page say nothing about it, and the FCDO refers vaccine questions to TravelHealthPro. Not a conflict: no official Kiribati source states a requirement.

entries.field: UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman and Qatar — visa-free stay
entries.old: 60 days per visit (cited to the MFA home page)
entries.new: 180 days in every 360-day period
entries.note: Not a conflict: the 60 days rested on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' home page, which does not state it. The Regulation on the stay of foreign citizens, as amended by Cabinet Resolution No. 855 of 31 December 2025 (current edition of 7 September 2026, read today in the Ministry of Justice's legal database), lets citizens of all six states stay visa-free for a total of 180 days in each 360-day period from entry, unless a treaty provides otherwise. The e-Visa portal's eligibility table (read today) gives ordinary passports 'up to 180 days'.

entries.old: Visa-free for up to 30 days, according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' e-Visa portal, which gives the 30-day regime to residents of the Hong Kong and Macao SARs and to citizens of the Maldives on all passport types.
entries.new: 30 days visa-free kept, now cited to paragraph 16 of the Regulation; the portal table's 'no visa-free regime' shown beside it
entries.note: The e-Visa portal's banner gives Hong Kong and Macao permanent residents a 30-day visa-free regime, but its own country table answers 'no' for Macao. Paragraph 16 of the Regulation on the stay of foreign citizens grants the 30 days in law, which outranks the portal. Resolved by hierarchy. Hong Kong is not in the table and is now cited to the same paragraph.

entries.field: Maldives — the e-Visa portal contradicts itself
entries.new: 30 days visa-free kept; the note now records that the portal's table says otherwise
entries.note: The portal's banner says citizens of the Maldives have a 30-day visa-free regime for all passport types; its country table answers 'no' for the Maldives. The same table also answers 'no' for Macao, whose 30-day regime is in the Regulation, so the table is out of date for exactly this kind of entry and loses to the banner's specific statement. No Kyrgyz legal text for the Maldives agreement could be read today (the Maldivian MFA page is behind a bot wall); flagged for a human to confirm.

entries.old: visa-free, unreconciled with the Foreign Ministry list
entries.new: visa-free kept, cited to Regulation (EU) 2018/1806; the ministry list shown beside it
entries.note: The Foreign Ministry's list of countries whose citizens may enter without a visa (updated 26 March 2026) omits Nauru. The consolidated Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 lists Nauru in Annex II (exempt). Law ranks above a ministry page. Resolved by hierarchy.

entries.field: Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bolivia, Colombia, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Guatemala, Honduras, Kazakhstan, Nicaragua, El Salvador, Turkey and the Holy See — entry requirement
entries.old: free one-month visa on arrival, extendable to three months
entries.new: visa from a Lebanese embassy or prior approval from General Security
entries.note: None of the thirteen is on General Security's list of nationalities given a visa at the border (Second Article, section one, in both the English and Arabic versions, read today); its Eleventh Article says citizens of countries not mentioned need a visa from a Lebanese embassy or prior approval from General Security. Colombia and Kazakhstan appear only for diplomatic and official or service passports; Ecuador is listed among labour-supplying countries needing prior approval; the Arabic version adds Kazakh women aged 17–45 to the one-month free visa for women. The Holy See's own page (posts/557) gives the automatic one-month visa to diplomatic and service passports only. The rows cited General Security's front page, which states none of this — not a conflict.

entries.old: visa on arrival with conditions such as accommodation, funds, or residence in a GCC or Western country
entries.new: one-month visa at the airport, extendable to three, with return ticket, hotel or address, and US$2,000; women need prior approval
entries.note: General Security's Eighth Article: 1-month visa extendable to 3 months for Egypt and other Arab states, with a return ticket, a hotel reservation or address and phone number, and US$2,000 or a certified cheque; exempt from the money with a visa from a Lebanese mission or General Security. Tenth Article: female citizens from Indonesia, Ghana, Sierra Leone or Egypt need prior authorization for tourism. The 'residence in a GCC or Western country' route is not on the page.

entries.old: free one-month visa on arrival, extendable to three months
entries.new: visa-free for three months with a national-number passport (extendable free to one year); the one-month route with conditions noted
entries.note: The page names Jordan twice. First Article: Jordanian citizens holding a passport with a national number who arrive as tourists are exempted from entry visas; the passport is stamped '3 months' free of charge, extendable to one year. Eighth Article (b): Jordan among nationalities given a one-month visa at the airport and border posts, extendable to three, subject to the US$2,000 condition. Ninth Article: the Jordanian passport issued to Palestinians is a pass needing prior approval. One source, and the First Article is expressly limited to national-number passports, so both are written into the note rather than one chosen; the headline follows the First Article.

entries.field: Angola, Guinea-Bissau, Mozambique, São Tomé and Príncipe, Timor-Leste and Ukraine — entry requirement
entries.new: visa on arrival, 30 days
entries.note: None of the six is on the portal's list of 88 nationalities exempted by the Chief Executive's written instruction, and none is among the six nationalities that must apply in advance, so the visa on arrival applies. The page also exempts nationals of countries with a mutual visa-free agreement with Macao but names none, and no official page names these six. For Angola, the Identification Services Bureau announced on 4 September 2026 (https://www.dsi.gov.mo/zh-hant/news/179) that a mutual visa-exemption agreement (30 days) was signed and that its entry-into-force date will be announced separately. No official source said the six were visa-free — not a conflict.

entries.field: Sudan, Somalia, South Sudan, Chad and Kosovo — entry requirement
entries.new: no visa required; length of stay not stated
entries.note: The Immigration Department's 'Visa requirement by country' page lists the countries required to apply for a visa (Afghanistan to Sri Lanka, India exempt until 31 December 2026), and the eVISA portal's FAQ says the eVISA 'is only compulsory for 31 specific nationalities' and gives the same list. Neither names these five. The rows cited the Immigration Department front page, which states nothing about them — not a conflict. Neither page states the stay granted, so it is left blank rather than guessed.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs' 'Ai-je besoin d'un visa pour voyager au Mali ?' check, run again today for each of the seven nationalities, answers 'Un visa vous est requis pour voyager sur le territoire Malien' (it still answers 'Vous n'avez pas besoin d'un visa' for Senegal). entries.field: Yellow fever certificate — conflicting official sources

The destination's own government ranks above an international compilation: resolved by hierarchy. The age threshold (1 year) was dropped because no source read today states one.

entries.field: Visa on arrival fee — conflicting official sources

entries.old: up to 90 more days (cited to migob.gob.ni, blocked)

No readable official source states 90 days, so this is a correction rather than a conflict.

entries.new: entry and use only with prior authorisation from the Ministry of the Interior, granted in special cases (Law 1230); UK advice calls possession and use prohibited

The FCDO says possession and use are prohibited and drones must be handed in. The law ranks above foreign travel advice (resolved by hierarchy); customs notes carry no source object, so both are stated in the text.

entries.old: 3 months beyond the stay, cited to the Foreign Ministry front page (which does not state it); the FCDO says 90 days after arrival
entries.new: 3 months beyond the stay kept, cited to the Foreign Ministry page that states it; the FCDO figure shown beside it

The FCDO says a British passport needs an expiry date at least 90 days after the date you arrive. The destination's own ministry ranks above another government's travel advice. Resolved by hierarchy.

entries.old: A yellow fever certificate is required only if you are arriving from, or have transited, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

Not a conflict: no official Palauan source states a requirement.

entries.field: 67 passports (US, Australia, New Zealand, EU/EEA, China and others) — conflicting official sources
entries.new: visa before travel on the paper visitor-visa form; the Visa Information Guide's 'applied for online' shown beside it
entries.note: ICSA's Visitor Visa page (read today) says travellers from visa-on-arrival countries 'may lodge an application via the electronic visa portal' and that those not eligible for a visa on arrival 'should submit their application using the paper form'. ICSA's Visa Information Guide (read today) also restricts both Easy Visitor Permits to 'passport holders from the eligible visa on arrival countries', but says applications in the visitor class 'must be submitted online'. None of these 67 nationalities is on the visa-on-arrival list. Same authority, and neither page is dated: the version that cannot strand a traveller wins (stricter). Summary, two FAQ answers and a tip reworded; flagged for review in case the portal does accept these passports for the Tourist (Own Itinerary) class.

entries.old: A yellow fever certificate is required for travelers aged one year and over arriving from, or having transited more than 12 hours in, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.
entries.new: any airport transit through a risk country counts, regardless of duration
entries.note: WHO's Annex 1 (read today) lists Papua New Guinea as requiring proof of vaccination from travellers aged 1 and over arriving from risk countries, with footnote 8: including travellers who transited through the airport of such a country, 'regardless of the duration of the transit'. The 12-hour figure is WHO's footnote 5, which applies to other countries. The fact was cited to ICSA's home page, which does not state it; the FCDO agrees that a certificate is needed when coming from a risk country.

entries.field: Visa-free stay, 79 passports — 183-day yearly cap replaced by the Foreign Ministry's per-country terms
entries.old: up to 90 days per entry, capped at 183 days in any 365-day period (extendable to the cap)
entries.new: 43 passports: 90 days, extendable once by 90 within 365 days of first entry; 32 (EU/Schengen, GE, RU, TR, UA): 90 days in any 180; BB, CR, HN, PA: 90 days within 365, not extendable
entries.note: Not a conflict: the rows already cited the Foreign Ministry's exemption table (16 July 2026, re-read today), which gives each nationality 90* (extendable once for an equal period within 365 days), 90** (not extendable) or 90*** (every 180 days). No official source cited or found states a general 183-day cap — Migraciones' tourist page gives 180 days a year only for Andean Community extensions. Summary and two FAQ answers corrected to match; Mexico, El Salvador, Qatar (183, not extendable) and the Dominican Republic (60) were already right.

entries.old: Visitors entering on the visa waiver should hold a passport valid for at least 6 months from the date of arrival. Hayya's e-visas (A1, A2, A3 and A4) require at least 3 months' validity from the date of arrival.
entries.new: 3 months from arrival for every visitor (Hayya; Qatar Tourism for visa-free entry); the FCDO's 6 months shown beside it
entries.note: Hayya's FAQ (read today) lists 'minimum of 3 months passport validity from the date of arrival' as a requirement for entry through Hayya, and Qatar Tourism's visas page (visitqatar.com) says the passport of a visitor entering visa-free or on arrival must be valid for at least three months from arrival. The UK Foreign Office says 6 months for anyone visiting. Hayya runs the procedure and outranks another government's travel advice: resolved by hierarchy.

entries.old: visa required (eVisa), kept on 26 September pending review
entries.new: visa-free with eTA; length of stay set by the immigration officer

A correction, not a conflict. The summary and FAQ now point to the ministry's list instead of saying everyone else needs a visa.

entries.old: certificate required when arriving from a risk country (cited to the government front page)
entries.new: no vaccination requirement (eTA platform); WHO's "required from risk countries, age 1+" shown beside it

WHO's International Travel and Health Annex 1 and the FCDO still list a certificate requirement for arrivals from risk countries. The destination government's own statement ranks above the WHO compilation and foreign travel advice. Resolved by hierarchy. The item stays, marked recommended, so the disagreement is visible.

entries.field: Arrival form timing — conflicting official sources
entries.old: any time before arrival, up to departure (2022 announcement); unreconciled with Canada's "within 3 days"

The Government's 28 November 2022 announcement said there was no time limit on early submissions. The portal runs the procedure and is current, so it ranks above the announcement (Canada's advice agrees with it). Resolved by hierarchy.

entries.old: visitor's visa in advance ("not on the visa-exemption list"), cited to the government's front page

Its Visitors' Permits page grants 'Other International Countries – three (3) months' on arrival. The front page these rows cited states no requirement, so no official source says these 24 need a visa: a correction, not a conflict. Kosovo's row (non-recognition) was left for review.

Same rank, neither dated; the 30-day stay cannot leave a traveller overstaying. Resolved as stricter.

The disagreement is not yet shown on the page: minv.sk is not in data/official-hosts.json, so it cannot be linked as the conflicting source. Value unchanged.

Its policy SC-PA-01-06 (revision 11, effective 1 July 2026) allows seizure of rand notes above R100,000 outside the Common Monetary Area. The FCDO still says declare over R25,000 or USD 10,000. Customs outranks foreign advice: resolved by hierarchy. The cited gov.za home page stated neither.

entries.old: certificate required when arriving from a risk country (cited mofa.gov.sd, which does not resolve)
entries.new: not required, recommended (Sudanese embassy); the FCDO's 'required of every traveller' shown beside it
entries.note: The Embassy of Sudan in Washington, read today: 'Yellow fever and cholera vaccinations are not required but recommended.' WHO's International Travel and Health Annex 1 (revised 3 January 2023) marks Sudan as a risk country with no certificate requirement for any arrivals, which agrees. The FCDO says 'To enter Sudan, you must have a certificate to prove you've had a yellow fever vaccination.' The destination's embassy outranks both the IGO compilation and foreign advice: resolved by hierarchy. No official source states the risk-country rule we published.

entries.field: Haitian passport holders — conflicting statements on the eVisa service

Same page, same rank, no usable date on either statement; the version that cannot strand a traveller at the border wins. Resolved by stricter.

entries.new: 6 months from the date of departure from Suriname (eVisa service); FCDO's 6 months after arrival shown beside it
entries.note: The eVisa and Entry Fee service, which runs the procedure for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, states 6 months from departure in its FAQs and on the business eVisa page; the UK FCDO (updated 10 December 2025) says 6 months after arrival. The authority running the procedure ranks above another government's travel advice. Resolved by hierarchy. The sentence that a renewed passport means a new application was dropped: neither source states it today.

entries.field: Ghana, Maldives, Fiji, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
entries.new: visa required: USD 50 ordinary eVisa or visa on arrival
entries.note: The guidelines contradict themselves: section 6 exempts Commonwealth nationals (except the UK, Canada, Nigeria, India, Pakistan, Australia and New Zealand), while section 7 lists these five nationalities (Saint Lucia and Saint Vincent as 'Saint Lucian' and 'Saint Vincentian') as eligible for visa on arrival. One page, one date, so there is no second source to record as a conflict; the rows now cite the guidelines and publish the version that cannot strand a traveller at the border, and say so in their notes. Rule applied: stricter.

entries.old: visa required: eVisa or visa on arrival
entries.new: visa-free
entries.note: Section 6 of the guidelines exempts nationals of SADC member countries except Comoros; SADC's member-state list (sadc.int) includes Angola and Madagascar, and neither appears in section 7 (visa on arrival) or section 8 (cannot obtain a visa on arrival). Nothing on the page contradicts the exemption for them.

entries.reason: Cameroon and Sri Lanka keep the eVisa or visa on arrival: both are Commonwealth members, which section 6 of the guidelines would exempt, but section 7 lists both for visa on arrival, and the stricter reading stands. Their rows now cite the guidelines instead of the portal front page and note the contradiction.

entries.field: EU citizens (26 member states, not Ireland) — conflicting official sources
entries.old: visa-free 90 days, cited to the Immigration Division's front page, unreconciled with its no-visa list
entries.new: visa-free up to 90 days in any 180 under the EU–Trinidad and Tobago short-stay visa waiver agreement; the Immigration Division list's omission shown beside it
entries.note: The Immigration Division's 'List of Countries Whose Citizens Do Not Require Entry Visas for TT' (September 2024) names 44 countries and no EU state. The agreement (OJ L 173, 3.7.2015; in force 1 May 2016 per OJ L 115, 29.4.2016), Articles 1, 2 and 4(1), gives citizens of every member state except Ireland visa-free stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period, and the Ministry of Foreign and CARICOM Affairs' notice 'Update to Short Stay Visa Waiver Agreement' (foreign.gov.tt/documents/6/short_stay_visa_waiver.pdf) says it is fully implemented. A treaty ranks above the authority's list. Resolved by hierarchy. The eVisa portal's nationality picker accepts German and French applicants but then states only that 'foreign nationals from a country requiring a visa can be processed online' — the same message it shows Indians — so it does not state a visa requirement and is not a conflicting source.

entries.new: visa required — eVisa (multiple entry, TTD 800) or visitor's visa from a mission
entries.note: Not a conflict: no official source states that Australians are visa-free. Smartraveller (updated 21 September 2026): 'You'll need an e-Visa to enter. The multiple entry e-visa fee is TTD800. Apply for your visa using the E-Visa Online Portal at least 14 business days before your travel.' Australia is absent from the Immigration Division's September 2024 no-visa list and the eVisa portal offers the nationality. The FAQ answer no longer lists Australia among visa-free nationalities. No stay length is stated, so maxStayDays is null.

entries.old: visa-free, up to 90 days (cited to the eVisa portal front page)
entries.new: eVisa before travel (USD 50 single entry, up to 90 days)

entries.old: 6 months on arrival (cited to the e-visa portal)
entries.new: 3 months after the date of arrival
entries.note: Not a conflict: the e-visa portal the 6-month rule cited (home page and 'What you need to know', read today) states no minimum validity, only that a valid passport must be presented. The UK Foreign Office states that the passport must have an expiry date at least 3 months after the date you arrive. No Uzbek official page found states another figure.

entries.field: Bahrain, Turkey, Rwanda and Monaco — conflicting statements on one official page
entries.old: Bahrain, Turkey, Rwanda visa-free 120 days; Monaco e-Visa
entries.new: e-Visa required (30 days) for all four; the double listing noted in each row
entries.note: The Department of Immigration's page (read today) lists all four under 'Countries not requiring a visitor visa (exempted countries)' and again under 'Countries requiring a visitor visa (non-exempted countries)'. One source, same rank, undated: the version that cannot strand a traveller wins — a visa over no visa. Resolved as stricter; the rows have no source of their own, so the note carries it.

entries.new: e-Visa required, 30 days
entries.note: Macao appears on neither list of the Department of Immigration's page (Hong Kong is on the exempt list). No official source states that Macao passports are exempt; the exempt list is the only basis for visa-free entry. Not a conflict.

entries.old: required for all; no fixed sum published (cited to the front page, which does not state it)
entries.new: visitor visa applicants: at least 40,000 vatu a month, or evidence of support in Vanuatu; no sum published for visa-exempt visitors
entries.note: The Department of Immigration's visitor visa page: 'Demonstrate funds or income to support the applicant for the duration of the stay (at least 40,000 vatu per month) or provide evidence of support from family/friends in Vanuatu.' The schema's per-person/day/trip units cannot hold a monthly figure, so the amount lives in the text. Not a conflict: no official page said no sum is published.

entries.field: Blank passport pages — conflicting official sources
entries.new: 3 full blank pages (Department of Immigration, visa on arrival); the FCDO's 2 shown beside it
entries.note: Zambia's Department of Immigration, which issues the visa, states at least 3 full blank pages for visa on arrival (read today); the FCDO's entry-requirements page (updated 1 June 2026) says 2. The authority running the procedure ranks above another government's advice. Resolved by hierarchy.

entries.old: visa on arrival, left unreconciled (cited to the portal front page)
entries.new: visa on arrival kept, cited to the Department's Category B page; the eVisa portal's Category C listing shown beside it
entries.note: Both lists come from the Department of Immigration (same rank). Its Category B page, which lists Bolivia, was last modified on 10 June 2025; the eVisa portal's FAQ, which puts Bolivia in Category C (visa before travel), carries a 'Last Published 27 March 2024' stamp and its text is unchanged from the Wayback Machine copy of 15 April 2025. The newer list wins. Resolved by newer.

entries.field: UAE passport — which emirates the Foreign Ministry names
entries.old: 'No visa needed for stays of up to 90 days' with no mention that the list names emirates
entries.new: notes say the Foreign Ministry's no-visa list names Dubai, Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah, not the UAE as a whole; Abu Dhabi, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain are not on it; advice to confirm with the eVISA office
entries.note: Re-read today (page last updated 2026.04.01). The accordion 'List of countries who does not need a visa' names 'Dubai', 'Sharjah', 'Ras Al Khaimah (RAK)' and 'Fujairah'; no emirate is on the visa-required list. The same page's country checklist marks 'United Arab Emirates' and 'Umm Al Quwain' as in the no-visa list (option values 'yes-'). Requirement and stay unchanged; the Department of Immigration conflict stays recorded.

entries.new: visa-free up to 90 days in any 180 under the Russia–Dominica visa-waiver agreement (cited to its official publication); the Government of Dominica page's omission (21-day tourist allowance only) recorded as the conflict
entries.note: Agreement of 28 September 2018 between the Governments of Russia and Dominica on the conditions for the waiver of visa formalities, in force 14 January 2019, officially published on pravo.gov.ru (eoNumber 0001201901160006). Article 1(1) (read today from the published scan): holders of valid passports of either state may enter, leave, transit and stay 'без виз до 90 календарных дней в течение каждого периода в 180 дней'. The Russian MFA consular department's Dominica page (kdmid.ru) says the same. The Government of Dominica's 'Do I Need a Visa' page does not list Russia, which on its own would leave only the 21-day bona fide tourist allowance. A treaty ranks above the destination's page. Resolved by hierarchy.

entries.old: cash sticker at airport kiosks; Cairo also sells a 36 USD digital visa since 1 August 2026
entries.new: adds that the Cairo visa is a QR code bought on the portal, the app or kiosks, valid seven days from issue and shown at passport control; Cairo is a pilot; applyUrl set to the Visa on Arrival portal
entries.note: Read today: the Visa on Arrival portal (apps.visaonarrival.gov.eg) describes the pay, create-QR-code, show-to-officer process, and the Cairo Governorate portal's news of 1 August 2026 says the QR code replaces the paper sticker, can be bought on the app, at Cairo kiosks or on the portal, is valid seven days, and is a pilot before other airports. FCDO (updated 4 August 2026) gives 1 August 2026 and 36 USD including a 6 USD fee. No official page gives a 1 September 2026 date or says every airport has switched, so the paper sticker at other airports stays.

entries.old: visa-free, 28 days, extendable (Commonwealth assumption, no source)
entries.new: embassy visa (visa and entry clearance)
entries.note: The Immigration Department's visa page, read today, lists South Africa under 'Countries That Need Both Visa And Clearance For African Countries'. The visa-free value rested on a general Commonwealth rule with no official source, and none stating it for South Africa was found, so this is a correction, not a conflict.

entries.old: about GYD 3,000 (approximate; cited to the Ministry of Home Affairs front page, which states no fee)
entries.new: GYD 5,125 for a three-month extension (GYD 28,700 if more than three months is granted); at most two extensions; applied for through Immigration Support Services
entries.note: Immigration Support Services' Visitor Visa Extension page (read today): 'The application processing fee for the Extension of Stay Visitor Visa is $5,125 GYD ... In a situation where an applicant is given an extension exceeding three (3) months, the processing fee will be $28,700 GYD. A maximum of two (2) Extension of Stay will be granted. Each extension will be a period of three (3) months.' No official source states the ~3,000 figure, so this is a correction, not a conflict. The FAQ answer on extending a stay was brought into line.

entries.reason: The consular tourist visa cited the INM front page (unreachable, portalOnly). The Honduran Embassy in London's visa page, read today, states 'Visa Sencilla (30 días): $30.00' and 'Visa Múltilple (90 días): $60.00', 'Visa Fees: Single: $30 USD / Multiple: $60 USD', and that tourists may stay 'un máximo de 90 días, prorrogables por otros nuevos 90 días más' at the INM — the visa type's 30-day single / 90-day multiple split, fee and 90-day extension. hondurasembassyuk.com is now a registered official host.

entries.old: 180 days, conflict with PICA's '90 days' described in the row's notes, no citation
entries.new: 180 days cited to the CARICOM communiqué (instrument: the Heads of Government six-month definite-entry decision); PICA's '90 days' recorded in source.conflict
entries.note: Communiqué (read today): 'Heads of Government welcomed the actions taken by Belize, Grenada, Guyana and Suriname to implement the decision that CARICOM nationals travelling to other Member States be granted a definite entry of six months ... They urged the other Member States to take the necessary actions to implement the decision.' PICA's table (last updated 19 July 2023), re-read today: 'SURINAME NO visa required for 90 days'. A decision of the Community's supreme organ ranks above a national immigration table. Resolved by hierarchy. The conflict sentence was removed from the row's notes now that the row carries its own source.

entries.old: embassy visa with Ministry prior approval, except listed groups (undated FAQ won, 'stricter')
entries.new: visa on arrival or e-visa, no prior approval, passport valid 3 months
entries.note: Both sides are the Ministry of Interior and were re-read today. Its FAQ (undated) still says Libyan nationals need prior approval unless resident in a non-restricted country, holding a Schengen/US visa, or a patient. Its decision of 27 October 2024 lets Libyans in without prior approval, with the visa online or at the border, and Libya is not on the Ministry's current list of restricted nationalities. Same rank, and only the decision is dated, so it wins (newer). The FAQ is shown as the conflicting source.

entries.path: visaPolicy.byPassport.SA, AE, KW, QA, BH, OM
entries.old: visa-free, 90 days ('commonly three months', no source)
entries.new: visa-free, 180 days (6 months, extendable to one year free)
entries.note: General Security's visa list, read today: the statement '6months' is stamped free of charge for GCC citizens ('3months' is for Jordanians), and the stay can be extended to one year free by the Department of Arabs and Foreigners. The 90-day value had no official source, so this is a correction, not a conflict.

entries.old: visa-free, 90 days (no source of its own)
entries.new: visa-free, 90 days, cited to the Accès Maroc eligibility check; Foreign Ministry list recorded as the conflicting source
entries.note: The Foreign Ministry's list of visa-exempt countries (consulat.ma, read today) marks Mali 'Besoin d'une AEVM'. The official eVisa portal's eligibility check, run today for a Malian ordinary passport resident in Mali, answers that no visa and no travel authorisation are needed. The portal is the authority that runs the procedure and ranks above the ministry list, so visa-free stands (hierarchy). The ministry's statement is shown beside it.

entries.old: visitor's visa ('does not recognize Kosovo'), cited to the government's front page, which states nothing on it
entries.new: visa-free; visitor's permit of up to 3 months on arrival, extendable
entries.note: The Ministry of National Security, which issues entry visas, names the only nationalities that must apply: 'Afghanistan, Cameroon, China, Dominican Republic, Haiti, Iran, Iraq, Lebanon, Nigeria and Syria' (read today); Kosovo is not among them, and the Visitors' Permits page grants other countries three months. No official source states that Kosovans need a visa or that their passports are refused, so this is a correction, not a conflict. Kosovo's MFA recognition list (mfa-ks.net/lista-e-njohjeve, read today) does not include Saint Vincent and the Grenadines; the row's notes mention it and point to the Immigration Department.

entries.old: visa-free, 90/180 (Reg. 2018/1806), disagreement described only in the changelog
entries.new: same value; Interior Ministry table recorded as the conflicting source
entries.note: minv.sk is now registered. The Interior Ministry's visa-free regime table (https://www.minv.sk/?bezvizovy-rezim, re-read today) still omits Micronesia and Nauru, and is stale: it still cites the 2022 suspension for Vanuatu passports. Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 Annex II lists both as exempt and wins (hierarchy). The table is now shown beside both rows.

entries.field: 93 passports on neither the no-visa list nor the EU agreement — entry requirement
entries.new: visa required — eVisa (multiple entry, TTD 800) or visitor's visa from a mission; cited to the Immigration Division's list
entries.note: The Immigration Division's 'List of Countries Whose Citizens Do Not Require Entry Visas for TT' (September 2024, re-read today) names 44 countries, none of these. The Division's eVisa portal (read today) says 'Only foreign nationals from a country requiring a visa can be processed online' and its nationality picker offers every one of these 93 nationalities while leaving out the 44 listed ones (and Irish); its FAQ (4 March 2024) says applicants must 'be a foreign national from a country requiring a Visa'. Official statements that these passports are visa-free were found for Japan (MOFA Overseas Safety, 25 March 2026: 90 days, on an answer from T&T's Foreign Ministry), Brazil (T&T Embassy in Brasília FAQ: 90 days), Türkiye and Serbia (foreign ministries: 30 days) and Colombia (Cancillería list, May 2026: no visa); each is recorded in source.conflict and loses to the authority running the procedure (hierarchy). Russia's MFA consular list (kdmid.ru, 3 July 2026: 90 days, unilateral) also disagrees but its host is not a registered official host, so it is not linked. Chile's consular table saying 'NO' is dated 29 January 2015 and was not used. Pages tried and silent or unreadable: travel.state.gov (bot wall; Wayback offline), NZ SafeTravel, Switzerland EDA, Norway regjeringen.no, Mexico SRE, Israel gov.il, South Africa DIRCO, Argentina, US Embassy Port of Spain; rows without any other statement say so in their notes. For the UAE, T&T's Foreign Ministry (29 September 2025) says the visa-exemption agreement starts with diplomatic and official passports, extending to ordinary ones later.

entries.field: South Korea passport — conflicting official sources
entries.new: visa-free, 90 days, cited to the Korea–T&T exchange of notes on visa abolition (treaty no. 1247, in force 15 October 1994); the Immigration Division list's omission recorded as the conflict
entries.note: Korea Law Information Center treaty text (read today), paragraph 1: nationals of either state holding valid passports may enter the other without a visa for stays not exceeding 90 days, provided they do not engage in paid activity; paragraph 2: longer stays or paid activity need a visa in advance. Korea's MOFA 0404.go.kr (as of September 2026) lists 'Trinidad and Tobago (90 days / agreement)'. A treaty ranks above the Immigration Division's list. Resolved by hierarchy.

entries.new: visitor's visa from a mission; Ireland's DFA 'no visa' recorded as the conflict
entries.note: Ireland is not on the Immigration Division's list and is excluded from the EU–T&T visa waiver. Ireland's Department of Foreign Affairs (updated 12 August 2026) says 'Irish citizens do not require a visa to enter Trinidad and Tobago'; foreign governments' advice ranks below the authority running the procedure (hierarchy). The eVisa portal's nationality picker does not offer Irish, so the row points to a mission or immigration.visas@gov.tt rather than the eVisa. Flagged for human review: the two Immigration Division signals (list and portal) point different ways for Ireland.

entries.old: EU, UK, US, Canada, New Zealand and most Commonwealth and Latin American countries visa-free
entries.new: the 44 listed countries, EU citizens except Irish (EU agreement) and South Koreans (bilateral agreement) visa-free; CARICOM six months; everyone else, including US, Australian, Japanese and most Latin American citizens, needs a visa
entries.note: Brought into line with the row changes above.

entries.new: not extendable
entries.note: The page contradicts itself — "sin posibilidad de prórroga", then a line on applying to Migraciones. Same page, same rank, no date to separate them: resolved by the stricter reading, which cannot leave a traveller overstaying on an extension that is refused.

entries.field: US, Japan, Brazil, Ireland, Türkiye, Serbia, Colombia
entries.old: visa required (absent from the 2024 no-visa list)
entries.new: visa-free — US and Japan 90 days, Brazil 90, Türkiye and Serbia 30, Ireland and Colombia no stay stated
entries.note: Earlier today these rows were switched to visa-required because the Immigration Division’s no-visa list does not name them. An omission is not a statement: each has an official source that says visa-free outright — the US State Department (archived 1 April 2026: a tourist visa is required only for stays longer than 90 days), Japan’s, Türkiye’s, Serbia’s, Colombia’s and Ireland’s foreign ministries, and for Brazil Trinidad and Tobago’s own embassy. The 27 EU and Korean rows no longer record the list’s silence as a conflict.
